G2Antenati.2.full: Madame Vámos had not aged: so, at least, everyone swore. The Circle of the Last Hour no longer hid. It had premises on the square, a band for funerals and two hundred members, and that year it bought the land behind the town hall to build a temple on.
G2Antenati.2.easy: Madame Vámos had not grown older: at least, that is what everyone said. The Circle of the Last Hour no longer hid. It had premises on the square, a band for funerals and two hundred members, and that year it bought the land behind the town hall to build a temple.
G2Antenati.2.short: Madame Vámos had not aged, and the Circle, now two hundred strong, bought land to build a temple.

G2Antenati.3.full: Of the woman in the wagon only the stories remained, and a curious habit: every now and then an eye drawn in charcoal appeared on the doors of the houses of {0}. No one admitted to drawing it, and no one rubbed it out. The Circle of the Last Hour, people said, still met; but no one knew where, or who belonged to it.
G2Antenati.3.easy: Of the woman in the wagon only the stories were left, and a strange habit: every now and then, on the doors of the houses of {0}, an eye drawn in charcoal appeared. No one said they had drawn it, and no one rubbed it out. People said the Circle of the Last Hour still met, but no one knew where, or who belonged to it.
G2Antenati.3.short: Of the woman in the wagon only stories remained, and charcoal eyes on the doors of {0}. The Circle still met, no one knew where.

G2Antenati.4.full: The knocking on the walls had stopped with the last funeral of the first generation, and for seventeen years the estate had been a house like any other: cold in winter, damp in summer, full of things no one dared throw away.
G2Antenati.4.easy: The knocking on the walls had ended with the last funeral of the first generation. For seventeen years the estate had been a normal house: cold in winter, damp in summer, full of things no one had the courage to throw away.
G2Antenati.4.short: For seventeen years the estate had been quiet, like any other house.

G2Antenati.5.full: Only the founder's bedroom had stayed as it was, by written wish: the bed with the shape of the body, the lamp, the chair beside the bed. In seventeen years the chair had moved closer to the bed until it touched it.
G2Antenati.5.easy: Only the founder's bedroom had stayed as it was, as he had asked in writing: the bed with the shape of the body, the lamp, the chair by the bed. In seventeen years the chair had crept closer to the bed until it touched it.
G2Antenati.5.short: Only the founder's room had stayed as it was. In seventeen years the chair had crept up to touch the bed.

G2Antenati.6.full: The founder's bedroom, cleared many years before, had become a laboratory like the others. Only the old chair, back from the kitchen who knows when, always stood in the same corner, facing the bed that was no longer there.
G2Antenati.6.easy: The founder's bedroom, cleared many years before, had become a laboratory like the others. Only the old chair, back from the kitchen who knows when, always stood in the same corner, facing the bed that was no longer there.
G2Antenati.6.short: The founder's room was a laboratory. But the old chair had come back, facing the bed that was gone.

G2Antenati.7.full: The first night the new heirs sleep there, the knocking begins again. But this time, after the knocking, come the voices; and they are voices each of them knows very well, because they belong to those who brought them into the world.
G2Antenati.7.easy: The first night the new heirs sleep there, the knocking starts again. But this time, after the knocking, the voices come. They are voices each of them knows very well: they are the voices of their parents.
G2Antenati.7.short: On the first night the knocking returns, and after it the voices: their parents' voices.

G2Antenati.8.full: Each player in turn reads their ancestor's message without showing it to the others. They may tell it, lie about it or keep quiet.

G2AntA.3.full: The voice comes before the knocking: a dense whisper, without pauses, that neither greets you nor asks how you are. It speaks of formulae, of proportions, of an error in the third notebook that must be corrected at once, at once, before it is too late. You recognise the voice of the one who brought you into the world, and you recognise the tone too: it is the same as on the nights when no one came out of the laboratory.
G2AntA.3.easy: The voice comes before the knocking. It is a fast whisper, with no pauses, that does not greet you or ask how you are. It talks about formulae, numbers, a mistake in the third notebook that must be fixed now, before it is too late. It is the voice of your father or your mother, and you know the tone too: the same as on the nights spent shut in the laboratory.
G2AntA.3.short: A whisper without pauses: formulae, numbers, a mistake to fix at once. It is your parent's voice, in the tone of nights in the laboratory.

G2AntA.4.full: "You finish it," it repeats. "You finish it, you finish it." At dawn your hand aches and there are three dense pages in a handwriting that is not yours.
G2AntA.4.easy: "You finish it," it says again and again. "You finish it, you finish it." At dawn your hand hurts and you have three full pages in handwriting that is not yours.
G2AntA.4.short: "You finish it." At dawn you have three pages in a hand not your own.

G2AntA.5.full: It is not knocking: it is a quick, irregular tapping, like fingers drumming on a table in impatience. Then the voice, feverish, halfway through a sentence begun who knows when: "...and the numbers don't add up, they never add up, but you'll make them add up..."
G2AntA.5.easy: It is not knocking: it is a fast, uneven tapping, like fingers beating on a table out of impatience. Then the voice comes, agitated, in the middle of a sentence started who knows when: "...and the numbers don't add up, they never add up, but you'll make them add up..."
G2AntA.5.short: An impatient tapping, then the voice: "...the numbers never add up, but you'll make them add up..."

G2AntA.6.full: You try to ask whether they are suffering. They do not listen; they never listened to you. When the tapping stops, you realise that you are drumming too, to the same rhythm, and cannot stop.
G2AntA.6.easy: You try to ask if they are suffering. They do not listen to you, just as they never did. When the tapping ends, you notice that you are tapping your fingers too, with the same rhythm, and you cannot stop.
G2AntA.6.short: They do not listen, as always. Then you notice that you are drumming too, and cannot stop.

G2AntA.8.full: There is only one knock, gentle, like a hand laid on the door. Then the voice, calm, almost amused: it asks whether you are eating enough, whether the greenhouse roof still leaks, whether you remember the miller's widow. "Tell her I'm well," it says.
G2AntA.8.easy: There is just one knock, soft, like a hand resting on the door. Then the voice, calm, almost amused: it asks if you eat enough, if the greenhouse roof still has holes, if you remember the miller's widow. "Tell her I'm well," it says.
G2AntA.8.short: One gentle knock, then a calm voice asking if you eat enough. "Tell the miller's widow I'm well."

G2AntA.9.full: You understand it is not speaking of itself. It is speaking of all the families it comforted in life, who now, on the other side, keep it company. Before leaving it blesses you, as it used to when you set off on a journey.
G2AntA.9.easy: You understand that it is not talking about itself. It is talking about all the families it helped in life, who now, on the other side, stay close to it. Before leaving it blesses you, as it did when you went on a journey.
G2AntA.9.short: The families it comforted in life now keep it company. Before leaving, it blesses you.

G2AntA.10.full: The room smells of warm bread and lavender: the smell of the estate kitchen, many years ago. The voice does not knock. It speaks softly, as at a sickbed, and tells you that it is not cold on the other side, and that the people it comforted in life came to welcome it.
G2AntA.10.easy: The room smells of warm bread and lavender: the smell of the estate kitchen, many years ago. The voice does not knock. It speaks softly, as next to a sick person's bed, and tells you that it is not cold on the other side, and that the people it helped in life came to welcome it.
G2AntA.10.short: A smell of warm bread and lavender. A gentle voice tells you it is not cold on the other side, and that it is not alone.

G2AntA.11.full: "You have time," it says. "Use it for the living." In the morning, on the bedside table, there is something that was not there the night before.
G2AntA.11.easy: "You have time," it says. "Use it for the living." In the morning, on the bedside table, there is something that was not there the evening before.
G2AntA.11.short: "Use your time for the living." In the morning there is a gift on the bedside table.

G2AntA.12.full: Gain $2 or 1 Knowledge of your choice.

G2AntA.13.full: The voice is low and wary, like someone speaking in a room where someone else is listening. "Listen carefully, because I won't be able to say it again. Many years ago I made a promise to the Circle, to a man with a black carnation. I thought I had sold something worthless. I was wrong."
G2AntA.13.easy: The voice is low and careful, like someone speaking in a room where another person is listening. "Listen carefully, because I won't be able to say this again. Many years ago I made a promise to the Circle, to a man with a black carnation. I thought I had sold something worth nothing. I was wrong."
G2AntA.13.short: A low, wary voice: "Long ago I made a promise to the Circle. I thought it was worth little. I was wrong."

G2AntA.14.full: Then it tells you what was promised, word for word, and who will have to open the door when the Circle knocks: you. "Tell no one," it ends. "But remember it. The day will come when you need to know how a promise is broken."
G2AntA.14.easy: Then it tells you exactly what was promised, and who will have to open the door when the Circle knocks: you. "Tell no one," it says at the end. "But remember it. One day you will need to know how to break a promise."
G2AntA.14.short: It tells you the promise, word for word: you will be the one to open the door. "Remember it. One day you must know how to break it."

G2AntA.15.full: Before the voice comes the smell: carnations and freshly dug earth. "The Circle is watching you," it whispers. "It watches all of us: those who signed and those born of those who signed."
G2AntA.15.easy: Before the voice comes the smell: carnations and freshly dug earth. "The Circle is watching you," it whispers. "It watches all of us: those who signed and those born to those who signed."
G2AntA.15.short: A smell of carnations and earth. "The Circle is watching you: those who signed, and their children."

G2AntA.16.full: It tells you of the envelope, of the pages written by a dead hand, of the promise to open a door. Then it tells you something the Circle does not know you know: the promise binds the blood, but the blood can choose not to keep it. At a price. What that price is, it has no time to say: the knocking stops halfway.
G2AntA.16.easy: It tells you about the envelope, the pages written by a dead hand and the promise to open a door. Then it tells you something the Circle does not know you know: the promise binds the whole family, but the family can choose not to keep it. There is a price, though. What it is, the voice cannot say: the knocking stops halfway.
G2AntA.16.short: The promise binds the blood, but the blood may choose not to keep it. At a price, which the broken-off knocking never names.

G2AntA.17.full: Gain 1 Occult Knowledge. The Storybook will remember this secret.

G2AntA.18.full: One knock, two, one: the same rhythm you heard told a thousand times at the table, by the voice that is speaking to you now. "That night I answered before anyone else," it says. "The door opened a little for me, and it never closed again."
G2AntA.18.easy: One knock, two, one: the same rhythm you heard described a thousand times at the table, by the voice that is speaking to you now. "That night I answered first," it says. "The door opened a little for me, and it never closed again."
G2AntA.18.short: One, two, one. "That night I answered first. The door opened a little, and never closed again."

G2AntA.19.full: Then, hurriedly, like someone afraid of being interrupted, it dictates to you the beginning of an experiment it never had the courage to attempt in life. You write until the candle burns out.
G2AntA.19.easy: Then, quickly, like someone afraid of being interrupted, it dictates the start of an experiment it never had the courage to try in life. You write until the candle is finished.
G2AntA.19.short: It hurriedly dictates an experiment it never dared try in life. You write until the candle dies.

G2AntA.20.full: The voice wastes no time on greetings. "You know how to answer, don't you? Once for yes, twice for no. I taught you, even if you don't remember: I used to tap on the side of your cradle, and you laughed."
G2AntA.20.easy: The voice does not waste time on greetings. "You know how to answer, don't you? Once for yes, twice for no. I taught you, even if you don't remember: I tapped on your cradle, and you laughed."
G2AntA.20.short: "You know how to answer, don't you? Once for yes, twice for no. I taught you, in your cradle."

G2AntA.21.full: A shiver. "I answered, the first night, and since then everyone over here can hear me. Now they can hear you too." When the voice falls silent, there is the outline of an experiment on the table, and on the bedroom wall there are knuckle marks, small ones, at the height of a cradle.
G2AntA.21.easy: You shiver. "I answered, the first night, and since then everyone here can hear me. Now they can hear you too." When the voice stops, there is the drawing of an experiment on the table. And on the bedroom wall there are small knuckle marks, at the height of a cradle.
G2AntA.21.short: "Since I answered, everyone over here can hear me. Now they hear you too." The outline of an experiment is left on the table.

G2AntA.22.full: Gain 1 {icon:Insanity_Icon} and draw an Experiment from the deck of your choice.

G2AntA.23.full: Distant, irregular knocking, like someone knocking at another house, in another street. You answer: nothing happens. You call out: the silence grows thicker.
G2AntA.23.easy: Distant, uneven knocking, like someone knocking at another house, in another street. You answer, but nothing happens. You call out, and the silence gets deeper.
G2AntA.23.short: Distant knocking. You answer, you call: only silence.

G2AntA.24.full: Perhaps the one who brought you into the world does not want to speak to you. Perhaps they cannot. Perhaps, you think with a relief you are a little ashamed of, they are simply resting in peace.
G2AntA.24.easy: Maybe your father or your mother does not want to talk to you. Maybe they cannot. Or maybe, you think with a relief that makes you a little ashamed, they are just resting in peace.
G2AntA.24.short: Maybe they will not speak to you. Maybe they are simply at peace.

G2AntA.25.full: You wait until dawn with the candle lit. You hear knocking on the walls of the other rooms, muffled voices, weeping, a laugh. On your wall, nothing.
G2AntA.25.easy: You wait until dawn with the candle lit. You hear knocking on the walls of the other rooms, faraway voices, crying, a laugh. On your wall, nothing.
G2AntA.25.short: Until dawn you hear knocks and voices in the other rooms. On your wall, nothing.

G2AntA.26.full: Only towards five does a very faint knock come, just one, which might mean yes, or might only be the wood settling in the cold.
G2AntA.26.easy: Only around five does a very soft knock come, just one. Maybe it means yes. Or maybe it is only the wood moving in the cold.
G2AntA.26.short: At five, one knock: perhaps a yes, perhaps the wood settling.

G2RispA.2.full: The voice falls silent, but does not go away. You can feel it waiting on the other side of the wall, patient, like someone who has asked a question and knows the answer will come. The candle has burned down to the saucer. Outside it is beginning to grow light.
G2RispA.2.easy: The voice stops, but does not go away. You can feel it waiting on the other side of the wall, patiently, like someone who has asked a question and knows the answer will come. The candle has burned down to the saucer. Outside it is starting to get light.
G2RispA.2.short: The voice stops, but waits for an answer. Outside it is getting light.

G2RispA.4.full: You knock once: yes, I am here.

G2RispA.5.full: You do not answer, and wait for it to leave.

G2RispA.6.full: You knock once, softly, with your knuckle. From the other side, after a very long silence, comes a single knock, light as a caress on the head. Then nothing more. For the rest of the night you sleep deeply, without dreams, as you have not done for years; and in the morning, on the wall, at the height of your pillow, there is the mark of a knuckle that is not yours.
G2RispA.6.easy: You knock once, softly, with your knuckle. From the other side, after a very long silence, comes a single knock, light as a hand stroking your head. Then nothing. For the rest of the night you sleep deeply, without dreams, as you have not for years; and in the morning, on the wall near your pillow, is the mark of a knuckle that is not yours.
G2RispA.6.short: You knock once. A knock answers, light as a caress. You sleep as you have not slept in years.

G2RispA.8.full: You lie still under the covers, holding your breath. The voice waits a little longer, then moves away, from room to room, like someone looking for another relative to talk to. At dawn the house is silent. You feel guilty, and at the same time lighter, like someone who has locked a door.
G2RispA.8.easy: You lie still under the covers, holding your breath. The voice waits a little longer, then moves away, room by room, like someone looking for another relative to talk to. At dawn the house is silent. You feel guilty, and lighter at the same time, like someone who has locked a door.
G2RispA.8.short: You do not answer. The voice leaves, room by room. You feel guilty, and lighter.

G2RispA.9.full: Move back 1 space on the {icon:Creepy_Icon} track.

G2AntFine.2.full: At dawn the voices fall silent. At breakfast the family is strangely courteous: the butter is passed, the weather discussed, and everyone avoids meeting anyone's eye.
G2AntFine.2.easy: At dawn the voices stop. At breakfast the family is strangely polite: they pass the butter, talk about the weather and no one looks anyone else in the eye.
G2AntFine.2.short: At breakfast everyone is polite, and no one meets anyone's eye.

G2AntFine.3.full: Each of them heard something. No one knows what the others heard. And all of them, at least for a moment, thought about lying.
G2AntFine.3.easy: Each of them heard something. No one knows what the others heard. And all of them, at least for a moment, thought about telling a lie.

G2AntFine.4.full: At the end of breakfast someone suggests:

G2AntFine.5.full: Writing down in the Journal what each of you heard.

G2AntFine.7.full: The Journal passes from hand to hand, on the breakfast table, among the crumbs. Each of you writes a few lines, and covers what they have written with a hand until they pass the notebook to their neighbour. At the end there are more handwritings on the page than there are people at the table.
G2AntFine.7.easy: The Journal goes from hand to hand on the breakfast table, among the crumbs. Each of you writes a few lines, and covers them with a hand until passing the notebook on. In the end there are more handwritings on the page than people at the table.
G2AntFine.7.short: Each of you writes in the Journal what you heard. In the end there are more handwritings than people at the table.

G2AntFine.9.full: The suggestion passes without any need for a vote. From that day on, at the estate, the dead are not spoken of at table, as money and illness are not spoken of. But in the evening, in the corridors, everyone walks a little closer to the wall, as if to hear better.
G2AntFine.9.easy: The idea passes without a vote. From that day, at the estate, the dead are not mentioned at table, just as money and illness are not. But in the evening, in the corridors, everyone walks a little closer to the wall, as if to hear better.
G2AntFine.9.short: No one speaks of the dead any more. But in the evening everyone walks close to the walls, to hear better.

G2R1.2.full: Open the Village Chronicle to the **Fear of the Unknown** section ({icon:S2_ScenarioIcon}) and turn to **page 4**.

G2R1.3.full: Open the Village Chronicle to the **The Cost of Disease** section ({icon:S1_ScenarioIcon}) and turn to **page 4**.

G2R1.4.full: {icon:Storybook} **The Temple of the Circle – Construction Site**

G2R1.5.full: When one of your pieces visits the Construction Site, pay $3 to fund the Temple of the Circle and

G2R1.8.full: When one of your pieces visits the Church, you may pay $2 for a mass for your dead:

G2R1.11.full: The first player who sends one of their pieces to the Laborer's Union

G2R1.26.full: In the second volume of the Journal, between a recipe and a farrier's bill, there is the drawing of a machine for talking with the dead.
G2R1.26.easy: In the second volume of the Journal, between a recipe and a blacksmith's bill, there is the drawing of a machine for talking to the dead.

round.G2R1.end.full: The Early Years of the Second Generation have ended.

G2Muri.2.full: The Laborer's Union meets in a smoky room above the smithy, with a long table, a rolled-up banner and a work register hanging on a nail. The smith, now, is Jóska: a man of thirty with broad shoulders, black hands and hair still singed on the forehead, as when he was a boy. It is he who hands out the work to the village masons.
G2Muri.2.easy: The Laborer's Union meets in a smoky room above the smithy, with a long table, a rolled-up banner and a work register hanging on a nail. The smith now is Jóska: a man of thirty with broad shoulders, black hands and hair still singed at the front, as when he was a boy. He is the one who hands out work to the village masons.
G2Muri.2.short: The smith is now Jóska, thirty years old, and he hands out work to the village masons.

G2Muri.3.full: He recognises you by your face, or perhaps by your name. "The one who brought you into the world gave me a coin, once," he says, "and asked me to teach them a game. I never forgot it."
G2Muri.3.easy: He knows you by your face, or maybe your name. "Your parent gave me a coin once," he says, "and asked me to teach them a game. I never forgot it."
G2Muri.3.short: "Your parent gave me a coin once. I never forgot it."

G2Muri.4.full: He recognises you by your name, and his smile fades. "Your mother, or your father, I don't remember which, had me slapped in front of the forge. I was six. Some things you don't forget."
G2Muri.4.easy: He knows you by your name, and stops smiling. "Your mother, or your father, I don't remember which, had me slapped in front of the forge. I was six. Some things you don't forget."
G2Muri.4.short: "Your parent had me slapped. I was six. You don't forget that."

G2Muri.5.full: In the register, between a roof to be redone and a chimney to be swept, there are many identical lines, all with the same heading: *Circle of the Last Hour – work on the walls*. Private houses, almost all belonging to widows. Jóska sees where you are looking, and closes the register.
G2Muri.5.easy: In the register, between a roof to be mended and a chimney to be swept, there are many identical lines, all with the same heading: *Circle of the Last Hour – work on the walls*. Private houses, nearly all of them widows'. Jóska sees where you are looking, and shuts the register.
G2Muri.5.short: The register lists many jobs of *work on the walls* for the Circle, in widows' houses. Jóska shuts it.

G2Muri.7.full: You offer him money to explain that work to you.

G2Muri.8.full: You hire him to check the walls of the estate.

G2Muri.9.full: You report him to Father Anzelm.

G2Muri.10.full: Jóska takes the money, counts it and asks for as much again. Then, quietly, he explains everything with a craftsman's contempt for an easy job.
G2Muri.10.easy: Jóska takes the money, counts it and asks for the same again. Then, quietly, he explains everything with a craftsman's contempt for an easy job.
G2Muri.10.short: Jóska wants double. Then he explains it all, with contempt.

G2Muri.11.full: Jóska refuses the money. Then, quietly, he explains everything, the way one returns a favour.
G2Muri.11.easy: Jóska will not take the money. Then, quietly, he explains everything, as a way of returning a favour.
G2Muri.11.short: Jóska refuses the money, and explains everything, as if repaying a favour.

G2Muri.12.full: A cavity in the wall, a hand's breadth wide, beside the widow's bed; a padded little hammer hanging from a rope; the rope going down to the cellar, where a boy paid two kreuzer a night waits for the signal. "One knock for yes, two for no," says Jóska, and for a moment he looks like the boy behind the forge again. "But I never worked at the estate. Your walls knock on their own. They did it when I was little."
G2Muri.12.easy: A gap in the wall, a hand's width, beside the widow's bed; a padded little hammer hanging from a rope; the rope running down to the cellar, where a boy paid two kreuzer a night waits for the signal. "One knock for yes, two for no," says Jóska, and for a moment he looks like the boy behind the forge again. "But I never worked at the estate. Your walls knock by themselves. They did it when I was little."
G2Muri.12.short: A gap in the wall, a hammer, a boy in the cellar. "But I never worked at the estate," says Jóska. "Your walls knock by themselves."

G2Muri.14.full: Jóska goes round the estate for a whole day, knocking on the walls with his knuckles and with the handle of his hammer, listening the way a doctor listens to a sick chest. The walls are solid, he says: brick and mortar, no cavities, no ropes.
G2Muri.14.easy: Jóska goes round the estate for a whole day, knocking on the walls with his knuckles and his hammer handle, listening the way a doctor listens to a sick chest. The walls are solid, he says: brick and mortar, no gaps, no ropes.
G2Muri.14.short: Jóska checks every wall in the estate. They are solid: no gaps, no ropes.

G2Muri.15.full: Only in the wall of the big bedroom, the one that was your grandfather's, does the hammer sound hollow. Jóska makes a hole, and inside there is a coil of copper wire, green with oxide, carefully wound round an iron core. Someone walled it in there, many years ago. On the core, scratched with the point of a nail, there is a number: 1848.
G2Muri.15.easy: Only in the wall of the big bedroom, the one that was your grandfather's, does the hammer sound hollow. Jóska makes a hole, and inside is a coil of copper wire, green with age, carefully wound round an iron core. Someone bricked it in there, many years ago. On the core, scratched with the point of a nail, is a number: 1848.
G2Muri.15.short: Only in your grandfather's room does the wall sound hollow. Inside is a coil of copper wire on an iron core, scratched 1848.

G2Muri.17.full: Father Anzelm listens, nods, and the following Sunday devotes half a sermon to the smith. The Circle stops giving him work; the widows stop greeting him; the masons look for another leader.
G2Muri.17.easy: Father Anzelm listens, nods, and the next Sunday gives half his sermon to the smith. The Circle stops giving him work; the widows stop greeting him; the masons look for another leader.
G2Muri.17.short: Father Anzelm preaches against the smith. Jóska loses his work and the village's respect.

G2Muri.18.full: Jóska says nothing to anyone. But when you pass the smithy, the hammer on the anvil beats a rhythm you know, slow and stubborn: one, two, one.
G2Muri.18.easy: Jóska says nothing to anyone. But when you pass the smithy, the hammer on the anvil beats a rhythm you know, slow and stubborn: one, two, one.
G2Muri.18.short: Jóska says nothing. But when you pass, his hammer beats: one, two, one.

G2Tubo.2.full: Mihály the gravedigger is still there, bigger and more bent, with a white beard and the same cap. He takes you to your grandfather's grave, the one with the brass tube, without your asking.
G2Tubo.2.easy: Mihály the gravedigger is still there, bigger and more bent, with a white beard and the same cap. He takes you to your grandfather's grave, the one with the brass tube, without being asked.
G2Tubo.2.short: Old Mihály takes you to your grandfather's grave, the one with the brass tube.

G2Tubo.3.full: The tube is open, and round the mound the grass is trampled. "They come at night," the gravedigger explains, "from all over the village. They talk into the tube. They say the old man takes messages to the other dead, like a post office." He shows you a tin box full of folded notes. "Some push them inside. I take them out in the morning. I don't read them."
G2Tubo.3.easy: The tube is open, and the grass around the grave is trampled. "They come at night," the gravedigger explains, "from all over the village. They talk into the tube. They say the old man carries messages to the other dead, like a post office." He shows you a tin box full of folded notes. "Some push them inside. I take them out in the morning. I don't read them."
G2Tubo.3.short: People come at night to talk into the tube: they say the old man carries messages to the other dead.

G2Tubo.4.full: The lead that closed the tube is still there. But it is no longer flush with the brass: it sticks out a finger's width, swollen and cracked, as if something had pushed it from below, patiently, for twenty-five years.
G2Tubo.4.easy: The lead that sealed the tube is still there. But it is no longer level with the brass: it sticks out a finger's width, swollen and cracked, as if something had pushed it from below, patiently, for twenty-five years.
G2Tubo.4.short: The lead in the tube sticks out a finger's width, cracked, as if pushed from below for twenty-five years.

G2Tubo.5.full: The cap of the tube is gone: they looked for it for a long time, after the fortieth day, and never found it. The bell, on the other hand, is there, and on windless nights, says the gravedigger, it rings.
G2Tubo.5.easy: The tube's cap is gone: they searched for it for a long time after the fortieth day and never found it. The bell, though, is still there, and on nights without wind, says the gravedigger, it rings.
G2Tubo.5.short: The cap is gone. The bell, says the gravedigger, rings on windless nights.

G2Tubo.6.full: The tube is closed, as the gravedigger closed it after the forty days. The brass has turned green. Mihály says that in twenty-five years nobody from the family has ever stopped to look at it.
G2Tubo.6.easy: The tube is closed, as the gravedigger closed it after the forty days. The brass has turned green. Mihály says that in twenty-five years no one from the family has ever stopped to look at it.
G2Tubo.6.short: The tube is closed and green. In twenty-five years no one from the family has come to look at it.

G2Tubo.8.full: You open the tube and listen.

G2Tubo.9.full: You have it filled with earth and mortar, for ever.

G2Tubo.10.full: The same cold rises from the tube, the same smell of wax. And a sound, this time, that is not a knock: the steady scratching of a pen on paper, far down below, like someone writing without stopping. Every now and then the pen stops, and you hear someone blowing on the ink.
G2Tubo.10.easy: The same cold rises from the tube, the same smell of wax. And this time a sound that is not a knock: the steady scratch of a pen on paper, far below, like someone writing without stopping. Now and then the pen stops, and you hear someone blowing on the ink.
G2Tubo.10.short: From the tube comes the sound of a pen writing, far below, without stopping.

G2Tubo.12.full: Mihály fills the tube with earth, then with mortar, then pours over it the holy water Father Anzelm gave him for the occasion. Finally, he takes off the bell and buries it beside the headstone.
G2Tubo.12.easy: Mihály fills the tube with earth, then mortar, then pours over it the holy water Father Anzelm gave him for the purpose. Last of all he takes off the bell and buries it beside the headstone.
G2Tubo.12.short: Mihály fills the tube with earth and mortar, and buries the bell.

G2Tubo.13.full: In the evening, at the cemetery, all is quiet. At the estate, on the other hand, for a whole week the knocking on the walls is faster and louder, like someone who has been locked out.
G2Tubo.13.easy: In the evening the cemetery is silent. At the estate, though, for a whole week the knocking on the walls is faster and louder, like someone locked out.
G2Tubo.13.short: The cemetery is silent. At the estate, for a week, the knocking sounds like someone locked out.

G2Tubo.14.full: Move back 1 space on the {icon:Creepy_Icon} track and gain 1VP.

G2Filo.2.full: Mayor Bódi, son of old Bódi, is a man of forty with a waxed moustache and a gold watch he keeps looking at. In the town hall courtyard are the coils of copper wire for the imperial telegraph line, which will reach {0} within the year; and the Mayor, so they say, is the only one who knows how many there really are.
G2Filo.2.easy: Mayor Bódi, old Bódi's son, is a man of forty with a waxed moustache and a gold watch he keeps checking. In the town hall courtyard are the coils of copper wire for the imperial telegraph line, which will reach {0} within the year; and the Mayor, they say, is the only one who knows how many there really are.
G2Filo.2.short: The new Mayor Bódi keeps the copper coils for the telegraph. Only he knows how many there really are.

G2Filo.3.full: "My father used to say your family pays well and asks no questions," he says, stroking his moustache. "It is a rare quality."
G2Filo.3.easy: "My father said your family pays well and asks no questions," he says, stroking his moustache. "That is a rare quality."
G2Filo.3.short: "My father said you pay well and ask no questions."

G2Filo.4.full: "My father told me about you," he says, without smiling. "And about a certain receipt. I hope your memory is shorter than his."
G2Filo.4.easy: "My father told me about you," he says, without smiling. "And about a certain receipt. I hope your memory is shorter than his."
G2Filo.4.short: "My father told me about you, and about a certain receipt."

G2Filo.5.full: "My father used to say your family sides with the priest," he says, with a raised eyebrow. "I wonder what use a telegraph is to the priest."
G2Filo.5.easy: "My father said your family sides with the priest," he says, raising an eyebrow. "I wonder what the priest wants with a telegraph."
G2Filo.5.short: "My father said you side with the priest. What does the priest want with a telegraph?"

G2Filo.6.full: He shows you the coils the way a merchant shows silk. One, he says, could easily go missing. Coils do go missing, in storerooms.
G2Filo.6.easy: He shows you the coils the way a merchant shows silk. One, he says, could easily get lost. Coils do get lost, in storerooms.
G2Filo.6.short: One coil, he says, could easily get lost.

G2Filo.8.full: You buy a coil under the counter.

G2Filo.9.full: You come back at night and take it yourself.

G2Filo.10.full: You refuse, and tell him so to his face.

G2Filo.11.full: The Mayor pockets the money without counting it. The coil arrives at the estate at night, on a council cart, driven by an usher in livery who raises his hat outside the gate.
G2Filo.11.easy: The Mayor pockets the money without counting it. The coil arrives at the estate at night, on a council cart, driven by an usher in livery who raises his hat at the gate.
G2Filo.11.short: The coil arrives at night, on a council cart.

G2Filo.12.full: If you can, pay $2: gain 2 {icon:Gears_Icon}. Otherwise gain 1 {icon:Gears_Icon}: the Mayor makes do with a promise.

G2Filo.13.full: You enter the town hall courtyard after midnight, with a sack and a dark lantern. The coil weighs as much as a man. As you drag it out, a first-floor window lights up: behind the glass is the Mayor in his nightshirt, who watches you, raises his candle in greeting and goes back to bed.
G2Filo.13.easy: You get into the town hall courtyard after midnight, with a sack and a dark lantern. The coil weighs as much as a man. As you drag it out, a first-floor window lights up: behind the glass is the Mayor in his nightshirt, who watches you, raises his candle in greeting and goes back to bed.
G2Filo.13.short: You steal the coil at night. The Mayor sees you from his window, raises his candle and goes back to bed.

G2Filo.14.full: The next day, in the storeroom register, the coil is recorded as "delivered to the estate, account settled".
G2Filo.14.easy: The next day, in the storeroom register, the coil is listed as "delivered to the estate, paid".
G2Filo.14.short: The register lists it as "delivered to the estate, paid".

G2Filo.16.full: You tell him your family does not buy council property under the counter. The Mayor laughs, looks at his watch and shows you to the door with great courtesy. The next day a short piece appears in the Gazette praising "the honesty of the notable families our town hall has the honour to serve".
G2Filo.16.easy: You tell him your family does not buy council property under the counter. The Mayor laughs, checks his watch and shows you out very politely. The next day the Gazette prints a short piece praising "the honesty of the notable families our town hall has the honour to serve".
G2Filo.16.short: You refuse. The next day the Gazette praises "the honesty of the notable families".

G2Stagno2.2.full: The council has decided to drain the park pond: too many mosquitoes, too many miasmas, too many accidents. The workmen open the sluice on a Monday morning, and for three days the water goes down, slowly, uncovering the black bottom, which stinks of leaves and iron. Half the village comes to watch, handkerchiefs over their noses.
G2Stagno2.2.easy: The council has decided to drain the park pond: too many mosquitoes, too many bad smells, too many accidents. The workmen open the sluice one Monday morning, and for three days the water slowly drops, uncovering the black bottom, which stinks of leaves and iron. Half the village comes to watch, handkerchiefs over their noses.
G2Stagno2.2.short: The council drains the park pond. Half the village comes to look at the black bottom.

G2Stagno2.3.full: On the bottom, in the mud, there are hundreds of things: coins, rings, locks of hair tied with ribbon, photographs, letters sealed in bottles. For thirty years the mothers and widows of {0} have thrown them into the pond, secretly, for their dead. In the middle, at the deepest point, there is a child's ice skate, its strap still buckled.
G2Stagno2.3.easy: On the bottom, in the mud, are hundreds of things: coins, rings, locks of hair tied with ribbon, photographs, letters sealed in bottles. For thirty years the mothers and widows of {0} have secretly thrown them into the pond, for their dead. In the middle, at the deepest point, is a child's ice skate, its strap still buckled.
G2Stagno2.3.short: In the mud lie thirty years of gifts for the dead: rings, letters, locks of hair. In the middle is a child's skate.

G2Stagno2.4.full: Someone in the crowd says Peti's name. The old mother, in the front row, looks at the skate without crying.
G2Stagno2.4.easy: Someone in the crowd says Peti's name. His old mother, in the front row, looks at the skate without crying.
G2Stagno2.4.short: Someone says Peti's name. His old mother looks at the skate without crying.

G2Stagno2.5.full: Someone in the crowd says Peti's name, and then looks towards you. In the village, some stories are not forgotten.
G2Stagno2.5.easy: Someone in the crowd says Peti's name, then looks at you. In the village some stories are never forgotten.
G2Stagno2.5.short: Someone says Peti's name, and looks at you. Some stories are never forgotten.

G2Stagno2.7.full: You collect the letters in the bottles and read them.

G2Stagno2.8.full: You ask the priest to bless the bottom and burn everything.

G2Stagno2.9.full: You collect the coins, before the others do.

G2Stagno2.10.full: The letters are addressed to the dead, and the dead have not opened them. You open them, one at a time, in the evening, in the laboratory. Wives telling their husbands about the harvests, mothers asking their children if they are cold, an old man apologising to someone for a quarrel in 1831. In the last bottle there is a single sheet, in a child's handwriting: *"I'm not cold."* The bottle was sealed with wax, and the wax is recent.
G2Stagno2.10.easy: The letters are addressed to the dead, and the dead have not opened them. You open them, one by one, in the evening, in the laboratory. Wives telling husbands about the harvest, mothers asking their children if they are cold, an old man apologising to someone for a quarrel in 1831. In the last bottle is a single sheet in a child's hand: *"I'm not cold."* The bottle was sealed with wax, and the wax is new.
G2Stagno2.10.short: You read the letters to the dead. In the last bottle, sealed recently, a child has written: *"I'm not cold."*

G2Stagno2.12.full: The priest blesses the bottom of the pond with bucket and sprinkler, under the hostile eyes of the widows, then has the letters, photographs and locks of hair heaped on the bank and sets fire to them. The smoke is sweet and heavy. The skate does not burn: they bury it in a corner of the cemetery, without a name. The widows do not forgive you. Their daughters, perhaps, will thank you one day.
G2Stagno2.12.easy: The priest blesses the bottom of the pond with his bucket and sprinkler, under the hostile eyes of the widows, then has the letters, photographs and hair piled on the bank and sets fire to them. The smoke is sweet and heavy. The skate does not burn: they bury it in a corner of the cemetery, without a name. The widows do not forgive you. Their daughters, perhaps, will thank you one day.
G2Stagno2.12.short: The priest burns everything. The skate will not burn: they bury it. The widows do not forgive you.

G2Stagno2.14.full: You stoop in the mud with a sack, alongside the village boys and a few shameless adults. The coins span thirty years of different minting, some of them silver. The widows watch you from the bank, in silence. That night, at the estate, the knocking on the walls is wet: it leaves small rings of water on the plaster.
G2Stagno2.14.easy: You crouch in the mud with a sack, alongside the village boys and a few shameless grown-ups. The coins come from thirty years of different mintings, some silver. The widows watch you from the bank, in silence. That night, at the estate, the knocking on the walls is wet: it leaves little rings of water on the plaster.
G2Stagno2.14.short: You gather the coins while the widows watch. That night the knocking leaves rings of water on the walls.

G2Fondamenta.2.full: There is commotion at the Builder's Office: digging the foundations of the Circle's Temple, the workmen have found a lead box, buried two metres down, under a squared stone.
G2Fondamenta.2.easy: There is a stir at the Builder's Office: digging the foundations of the Circle's Temple, the workmen have found a lead box, buried two metres down, under a squared stone.
G2Fondamenta.2.short: Digging for the Circle's Temple, the workmen find a lead box.

G2Fondamenta.3.full: There is commotion at the Builder's Office: digging the foundations of the new post office, the workmen have found a lead box, buried two metres down, under a squared stone.
G2Fondamenta.3.easy: There is a stir at the Builder's Office: digging the foundations of the new post office, the workmen have found a lead box, buried two metres down, under a squared stone.
G2Fondamenta.3.short: Digging for the new post office, the workmen find a lead box.

G2Fondamenta.4.full: The foreman keeps it on the table as if it were a bomb. On the lid, scratched with a nail, are a date and three letters: *1828 – C. U. O.* Nobody has the courage to open it. Someone thought of calling the family from the estate, who "know about these things".
G2Fondamenta.4.easy: The foreman keeps it on the table as if it were a bomb. On the lid, scratched with a nail, are a date and three letters: *1828 – C. U. O.* No one dares open it. Someone thought of calling the family from the estate, who "know about these things".
G2Fondamenta.4.short: On the lid is scratched *1828 – C. U. O.* No one dares open it, so they call you.

G2Fondamenta.7.full: You hand it over to the Circle, unopened.

G2Fondamenta.8.full: You have it reburied, after having it blessed.

G2Fondamenta.9.full: Inside, on a bed of rotted velvet, are three locks of hair tied with black ribbon: one brown, one black, one fair. Beside them, a silver bell with no clapper. And a folded sheet, with three signatures and a sentence: *"Whoever leaves first, knock."* One of the signatures is the one you find every evening on the first page of the Journal.
G2Fondamenta.9.easy: Inside, on a bed of rotten velvet, are three locks of hair tied with black ribbon: one brown, one black, one fair. Beside them, a silver bell with no clapper. And a folded sheet, with three signatures and one sentence: *"Whoever leaves first, knock."* One of the signatures is the one you see every evening on the first page of the Journal.
G2Fondamenta.9.short: Inside are three locks of hair and a sheet with three signatures: *"Whoever leaves first, knock."* One is the Journal's.

G2Fondamenta.11.full: You take the box, unopened, to the Circle's house. You are received by a tall gentleman with a black carnation, who takes it in his hands the way one takes a newborn. "We thought we had lost it," he says. "Thank you. Your grandfather would be pleased." He sees you to the door, and at the door puts an envelope into your hand. Inside is money, and a lock of brown hair, tied with black ribbon.
G2Fondamenta.11.easy: You take the box, unopened, to the Circle's house. A tall gentleman with a black carnation receives you, and takes it in his hands as one holds a newborn baby. "We thought we had lost it," he says. "Thank you. Your grandfather would be pleased." He walks you to the door, and there puts an envelope in your hand. Inside are some money and a lock of brown hair, tied with black ribbon.
G2Fondamenta.11.short: The gentleman with the black carnation thanks you: "Your grandfather would be pleased." He gives you an envelope with money and a lock of hair.

G2Fondamenta.13.full: The priest blesses the box without opening it, with a grimace, and the workmen rebury it in a corner of the cemetery, under a stone. That night, at the estate, the knocks on the walls come in threes, always three, in three different places in the house, like three people looking for each other and not finding each other.
G2Fondamenta.13.easy: The priest blesses the box without opening it, with a grimace, and the workmen bury it again in a corner of the cemetery, under a stone. That night, at the estate, the knocks come in threes, always three, in three different places in the house, like three people looking for each other and never meeting.
G2Fondamenta.13.short: The box is buried. That night there is knocking in three places in the house, like three people looking for each other.

G2Tempio.2.full: You pay the masons in cash, in front of everyone. The Temple's foundations rise quickly, more quickly than they should: the masons say that at night someone works in their place, and that in the morning they find the stones already squared.
G2Tempio.2.easy: You pay the builders in cash, in front of everyone. The Temple's foundations grow fast, too fast: the builders say that at night someone works in their place, and that in the morning they find the stones already cut.
G2Tempio.2.short: You pay the masons. The Temple rises too fast: at night, they say, someone works in their place.

G2Tempio.3.full: Madame Vámos comes to see the building site. She shakes your hand and calls you by name in front of everyone, as one does with family. That evening the widows of the Circle light a candle for your dead.
G2Tempio.3.easy: Madame Vámos comes to see the building site. She shakes your hand and calls you by name in front of everyone, as people do with family. That evening the widows of the Circle light a candle for your dead.
G2Tempio.3.short: Madame Vámos calls you by name in front of everyone, and the Circle's widows light a candle for your dead.

G2Messa.2.full: Old Father Anzelm says a mass for your family's dead, in the empty church, with a single altar boy who yawns. At the end he takes you by the arm, with a strength you did not expect. "I buried them all, your people," he says. "Let them stay where I put them."
G2Messa.2.easy: Old Father Anzelm says a mass for your family's dead, in the empty church, with only one altar boy, who yawns. At the end he takes your arm, with a strength you did not expect. "I buried them all, your family," he says. "Let them stay where I put them."
G2Messa.2.short: After mass, old Father Anzelm grips your arm: "I buried them all, your people. Let them stay where I put them."

G2Messa.3.full: That night, for the first time in months, no one knocks in your room, and you sleep until broad daylight.
G2Messa.3.easy: That night, for the first time in months, no one knocks in your room, and you sleep until it is full daylight.

G2Messa.4.full: Move back 1 space on the {icon:Insanity_Icon} track.

G2Telegrafo.3.full: In the second volume of the Journal, between a recipe for preserving tissue and a farrier's bill, I found the design. Three plates drawn in Indian ink, with a care Grandfather gave to nothing else. He calls it the **Telegraph of the Dead**.
G2Telegrafo.3.easy: In the second volume of the Journal, between a recipe for preserving tissue and a blacksmith's bill, I found the design. There are three drawings in ink, made with a care Grandfather gave to nothing else. He calls it the **Telegraph of the Dead**.
G2Telegrafo.3.short: In the Journal I found Grandfather's design, drawn with rare care: the **Telegraph of the Dead**.

G2Telegrafo.4.full: A battery of glass jars; miles of copper wire wound around a soft-iron core; a keyboard of twenty-six bone keys; and at its centre a needle suspended in a flask full of a gas he calls "veil air". According to his calculations the dead do not speak: they alter the current, ever so slightly. A sensitive enough needle is all it takes to read them.
G2Telegrafo.4.easy: There are glass jars connected together, miles of copper wire wound around a piece of iron, a keyboard of twenty-six bone keys. In the middle there is a needle inside a flask full of a gas he calls "veil air". According to his calculations the dead do not speak: they change the electric current, very slightly. A very sensitive needle is enough to read them.
G2Telegrafo.4.short: Glass jars, copper wire, a bone keyboard and a needle in a flask of "veil air". The dead, he believed, barely move the current: a sensitive needle can read them.

G2Telegrafo.5.full: In the margin of the third plate there is a note in pencil: *"I did not have the time. They will."* Building the first stage requires gears, many more than we have in the house. Each of us will have to decide how much work to take away from our own experiments.
G2Telegrafo.5.easy: On the edge of the third drawing there is a note in pencil: *"I did not have the time. They will."* To build the first part we need many gears, many more than we have in the house. Each of us will have to decide how much work to take away from our own experiments.
G2Telegrafo.5.short: In the margin, in pencil: *"I did not have the time. They will."* It needs gears, and each of us must decide how many to spare.

G2Telegrafo.6.full: Jóska the smith, when I show him the drawings, studies them without touching them, his hands behind his back. Then he says he has seen the soft-iron core in the drawing before: it is the one he found walled into the wall of the big bedroom, with the number 1848 scratched on it.
G2Telegrafo.6.easy: When I show Jóska the smith the drawings, he studies them without touching them, his hands behind his back. Then he says he has seen the soft-iron core in the drawing before: it is the one he found bricked into the wall of the big bedroom, with the number 1848 scratched on it.
G2Telegrafo.6.short: Jóska recognises in the drawing the iron core he found in the wall, the one marked 1848.

G2Telegrafo.7.full: Copper, at least, is not lacking: the imperial telegraph coil is in the cellar, wrapped in a cloth, and nobody at the town hall has ever come looking for it.
G2Telegrafo.7.easy: At least there is no shortage of copper: the imperial telegraph coil is in the cellar, wrapped in a cloth, and no one at the town hall has ever looked for it.
G2Telegrafo.7.short: There is copper: the telegraph coil is in the cellar.

G2TelegrafoOfferta.2.full: Each player secretly takes in hand as many {icon:Gears_Icon} as they wish to offer, even none. When everyone is ready, reveal your offers together.

G2TelegrafoEsito.2.full: How many {icon:Gears_Icon} did you offer in total?

G2TelegrafoEsito.3.full: The first stage of the Telegraph takes up an entire wall of the laboratory. On the night they switch it on, the glass jars hum, the lamps dim throughout the house and the needle, in its flask, begins to tremble.
G2TelegrafoEsito.3.easy: The first part of the Telegraph takes up a whole wall of the laboratory. On the night they switch it on, the glass jars hum, the lights in the whole house get dimmer and the needle, inside the flask, starts to shake.
G2TelegrafoEsito.3.short: The Telegraph fills a whole wall. When they switch it on, the lights dim and the needle begins to tremble.

G2TelegrafoEsito.4.full: It is not the trembling of the current: it is slower, more stubborn, like a finger searching for a letter on a keyboard. It stops on a bone key. Then on another. Before anyone can read the word, a fuse blows, and in the dark, for a moment, someone laughs.
G2TelegrafoEsito.4.easy: It is not shaking because of the current: it moves more slowly and more surely, like a finger looking for a letter on a keyboard. It stops on a bone key. Then on another. Before anyone can read the word, a fuse blows, and in the dark, for a moment, someone laughs.
G2TelegrafoEsito.4.short: The needle seeks letters, key by key. Before the word can be read a fuse blows, and in the dark someone laughs.

G2TelegrafoEsito.5.full: The offered {icon:Gears_Icon} return to the supply. Whoever offered the most gains 3VP (in case of a tie, all tied players do).

G2TelegrafoEsito.6.full: The gears collected are barely enough for the base. The design goes back into the drawer, under the second volume of the Journal, and the pieces go back to those who offered them.
G2TelegrafoEsito.6.easy: The gears collected are only just enough for the base. The design goes back in the drawer, under the second volume of the Journal, and the pieces go back to the people who gave them.
G2TelegrafoEsito.6.short: There are not enough gears. The design goes back into the drawer.

G2TelegrafoEsito.7.full: That night the knocking on the walls is slower than usual, almost dragging. If the dead can be disappointed, they are.
G2TelegrafoEsito.7.easy: That night the knocking on the walls is slower than usual, almost tired. If the dead can be disappointed, they are.

G2TelegrafoEsito.8.full: The offered {icon:Gears_Icon} return to the players.

G2Nebbia.3.full: **THE FOG WILL NOT LIFT.** For eleven days a dense, whitish fog has covered {0} from dawn to dusk, and from dusk to dawn. The district doctor speaks of miasmas from the pond; the apothecary, of fumes from the estate; Father Anzelm, of a punishment. Lanterns light no further than three paces. Yesterday the coach arrived six hours late: the coachman swears he drove in circles around the cemetery all night.
G2Nebbia.3.easy: **THE FOG WILL NOT LIFT.** For eleven days a thick white fog has covered {0} day and night. The doctor says it comes from the pond, the chemist says it comes from the estate, Father Anzelm says it is a punishment. Lanterns light only three steps ahead. Yesterday the coach arrived six hours late: the driver swears he went round and round the cemetery all night.
G2Nebbia.3.short: **THE FOG WILL NOT LIFT.** For eleven days fog has covered {0} day and night. The coach circled the cemetery all night.

G2Nebbia.4.full: Stranger still are the accounts this newspaper continues to receive. Mrs Tóth saw her husband, nine years dead, waiting for her at the corner by the apothecary. The baker heard his mother calling him from the oven. Three children played all afternoon with a friend none of the adults saw, and whose name no one knows. Readers are advised not to go out unless necessary, and not to answer anyone who calls their name from the fog.
G2Nebbia.4.easy: Even stranger are the stories that reach the newspaper. Mrs Tóth saw her husband, dead for nine years, waiting for her at the corner by the chemist's. The baker heard his mother calling him from the oven. Three children played all afternoon with a friend no adult saw, and whose name no one knows. We advise readers not to go out unless they must, and not to answer anyone who calls their name from the fog.
G2Nebbia.4.short: The dead are seen in the fog: a husband nine years buried, a mother calling from the oven, a nameless child. Do not answer anyone who calls you from the fog.

G2Nebbia.5.full: Some readers connect the fog with the draining of the park pond. Where there was water, they say, there is now a hole; and holes, in {0}, always fill up with something else.
G2Nebbia.5.easy: Some readers link the fog to the draining of the park pond. Where there was water, they say, there is now a hole; and in {0} holes always fill up with something else.
G2Nebbia.5.short: Some link the fog to the drained pond: in {0} holes always fill up with something else.

G2Nebbia.6.full: Old Mihály the gravedigger, finally, assures us that every evening the fog starts from the same spot: from the grave of the first master of the estate, the one with the brass tube.
G2Nebbia.6.easy: Finally, old Mihály the gravedigger swears that every evening the fog starts from the same spot: the grave of the first master of the estate, the one with the brass tube.
G2Nebbia.6.short: The gravedigger says the fog starts every evening from the grave with the brass tube.

G2Nebbia.7.full: At the estate, on the first evening of fog:

G2Nebbia.9.full: You bar the doors and windows.

G2Nebbia.10.full: You go out into the garden with lanterns, all together, holding hands like children. Three steps from the door the house disappears. Ten steps on you disappear too, from one another, and only your voices remain, calling each other by name. Too many answer. You come back in after an hour, counting yourselves on the threshold, and the count is right. Luckily.
G2Nebbia.10.easy: You go out into the garden with lanterns, all together, holding hands like children. Three steps from the door the house disappears. Ten steps further you disappear too, from each other, and only your voices remain, calling each other's names. Too many voices answer. You come back after an hour, count yourselves at the door, and the number is right. Fortunately.
G2Nebbia.10.short: You go out into the fog. You call each other's names, and too many answer. Back inside you count yourselves: luckily, you are all there.

G2Nebbia.12.full: You close the shutters, bar the doors, stop the cracks with wet rags. The fog stays outside, against the panes, white and patient like an animal waiting to be let in. Towards midnight someone knocks at the front door, three times, politely. Nobody goes to open it. In the morning, on the doorstep, there are wet footprints, that arrive and do not leave.
G2Nebbia.12.easy: You close the shutters, bar the doors, stuff the cracks with wet rags. The fog stays outside, against the glass, white and patient like an animal waiting to come in. Around midnight someone knocks at the front door, three times, politely. No one goes to open it. In the morning there are wet footprints on the doorstep, coming but not going.
G2Nebbia.12.short: You bar everything. At midnight someone knocks three times at the door. In the morning there are footprints coming but not going.

G2Nebbia.14.full: From the **The Cost of Disease** Scenario Box, take the **Creepy tokens** {icon:Creepy_Icon}: they are the **Presences**.

G2Nebbia.15.full: Place one {icon:Creepy_Icon} token on the **Cemetery**, one on the **Fortune Teller** and one on the **Hospital**.

G2Nebbia.16.full: Place one {icon:Creepy_Icon} token on the **Cemetery** and one on the **Fortune Teller**.

G2Nebbia.17.full: When a player takes an action at a Location with Presences, they gain 1 {icon:Creepy_Icon} for each {icon:Creepy_Icon} token on that Location.

G2R2.8.full: Father Anzelm treats the "possessed" in the Asylum Program. When one of your pieces visits it,
