G2R2.26.full: In the fog the veil is as thin as wet paper. Someone means to take advantage of it.
G2R2.26.easy: In the fog the veil is as thin as wet paper. Someone wants to use it for their own good.

round.G2R2.end.full: The Middle Years of the Second Generation have ended.

G2Gioco.2.full: In the fog the cemetery has no edges: the headstones emerge from the white one at a time, like teeth, and the low wall cannot be seen. Somewhere among the graves, children are playing hide-and-seek. You hear the counting, the laughter, the footsteps running on the gravel. There are five of them. Then, when they call each other by name, there are six.
G2Gioco.2.easy: In the fog the cemetery has no edges: the headstones come out of the white one by one, like teeth, and the low wall cannot be seen. Somewhere among the graves children are playing hide-and-seek. You hear the counting, the laughter, feet running on the gravel. There are five of them. Then, when they call each other by name, there are six.
G2Gioco.2.short: In the foggy cemetery children play hide-and-seek. There are five. When they call their names, there are six.

G2Gioco.3.full: The sixth is eight years old, with wet clothes and rosy cheeks. None of the others knows his name; they say he comes to play only when there is fog, and that he is the best of all at hiding.
G2Gioco.3.easy: The sixth is eight years old, with wet clothes and pink cheeks. None of the others knows his name; they say he only comes to play when there is fog, and that he is the best of all at hiding.
G2Gioco.3.short: The sixth is eight, with wet clothes. He only comes with the fog, and he is the best at hiding.

G2Gioco.4.full: You see him disappear behind a small headstone with a stone angel: the headstone your family paid for, many years ago, for the cooper's son.
G2Gioco.4.easy: You see him vanish behind a small headstone with a stone angel: the one your family paid for, many years ago, for the cooper's son.
G2Gioco.4.short: You see him vanish behind the angel headstone your family paid for, for the cooper's son.

G2Gioco.5.full: You see him searching among the graves, one by one, reading the names with his finger. A child asks him what he is looking for. "Mine," he answers. "I can't find it."
G2Gioco.5.easy: You see him searching the graves one by one, reading the names with his finger. A child asks what he is looking for. "Mine," he answers. "I can't find it."
G2Gioco.5.short: You see him searching the graves. "Mine," he says. "I can't find it."

G2Gioco.6.full: A sentence comes back to you, who knows why, one you have heard told in the family: a medium, a vigil, a child who "will play with the other children again, when the fog comes".
G2Gioco.6.easy: Something comes back to you, who knows why, a story told in your family: a medium, a vigil, a child who "will play with the others again, when the fog comes".
G2Gioco.6.short: You remember a family story: a child who "will play with the others again, when the fog comes".

G2Gioco.10.full: You call the sixth child over and ask him who he is.

G2Gioco.11.full: You count to fifty with your forehead against a headstone, as in childhood. You find them all, one after another, except him. You look for him until the fog turns grey, then blue, then black. In the end it is he who finds you: a small hand, cold as January water, touches your shoulder. "Found you," he says, and laughs. When you turn round there is nobody there, and your clothes are wet to the elbow.
G2Gioco.11.easy: You count to fifty with your forehead against a headstone, as when you were small. You find them all, one after another, except him. You look for him until the fog turns grey, then blue, then black. In the end he finds you: a small hand, cold as January water, touches your shoulder. "Found you," he says, and laughs. When you turn round there is no one there, and your clothes are wet up to the elbow.
G2Gioco.11.short: You play, and cannot find him. In the end a cold hand touches your shoulder: "Found you." You turn: no one. You are wet to the elbow.

G2Gioco.13.full: You gather the children and take them back to the village, one by one, to their mothers. The mothers thank you, then look at their children, then at the fog behind you, and close the door faster than necessary. Of the children, you brought back five. Nobody asks you about the sixth.
G2Gioco.13.easy: You gather the children and take them back to the village, one at a time, to their mothers. The mothers thank you, then look at their children, then at the fog behind you, and shut the door faster than they need to. You brought back five children. No one asks about the sixth.
G2Gioco.13.short: You take the children home: five of them. No one asks about the sixth.

G2Gioco.15.full: The child comes up to you without fear and tells you his name: Peti. Then he asks you about his mother. She is old now, and lives alone behind the cooper's workshop; you tell him, and he nods, as if he already knew. "Tell her I'm not cold any more," he says. "You tell her: she can't hear me."
G2Gioco.15.easy: The child comes up to you without fear and tells you his name: Peti. Then he asks you about his mother. She is old now, and lives alone behind the cooper's workshop; you tell him, and he nods, as if he already knew. "Tell her I'm not cold any more," he says. "You tell her: she can't hear me."
G2Gioco.15.short: "I'm Peti. Tell my mother I'm not cold any more. You tell her: she can't hear me."

G2Gioco.16.full: You go to the old woman that same evening. She does not ask you how you know. She sits you down, pours you a drink and listens to everything without crying. When you leave, the fog has lifted.
G2Gioco.16.easy: You go to the old woman that same evening. She does not ask how you know. She sits you down, pours you a drink and listens to it all without crying. When you leave, the fog has lifted.
G2Gioco.16.short: You tell his mother. She listens without crying. When you leave, the fog has lifted.

G2Fotografo.2.full: Next to the fortune teller's stall there is a new black tent, with a hand-painted sign: **HARTMANN – SPIRIT PHOTOGRAPHY – VIENNA, PARIS, LONDON**. Mr Hartmann is a small, kindly man, with fingers stained by silver nitrate. In front of the tent he has hung his portraits: widows, soldiers, children in stiff poses; and behind them, blurred and transparent, their dead, with a hand resting on the shoulder of the living.
G2Fotografo.2.easy: Next to the fortune teller's stall is a new black tent, with a hand-painted sign: **HARTMANN – SPIRIT PHOTOGRAPHY – VIENNA, PARIS, LONDON**. Mr Hartmann is a small, kind man, with fingers stained by silver nitrate. In front of the tent hang his portraits: widows, soldiers, children in stiff poses; and behind them, blurred and see-through, their dead, with a hand on the shoulder of the living.
G2Fotografo.2.short: Mr Hartmann does **SPIRIT PHOTOGRAPHY**: in his portraits, behind the living, stand their dead.

G2Fotografo.3.full: "With this fog," he says, "the plates come out as they never have before. The veil is thin here: my camera feels it." He looks at you with the professional eye of someone measuring up a pose. "And you, now, have quite a few dead in the family."
G2Fotografo.3.easy: "With this fog," he says, "the plates come out as never before. The veil is thin here: my camera feels it." He looks at you with the eye of someone working out a pose. "And you have quite a few dead in the family."
G2Fotografo.3.short: "With the fog the plates come out wonderfully. And you have plenty of dead in the family."

G2Fotografo.7.full: You pay him to teach you how he does it.

G2Fotografo.8.full: You stay still for a whole minute, your neck held in the iron clamp, while the photographer counts aloud. The portrait is ready two days later. There you are, back stiff and face pale; and behind you, only a little lighter than the fog, is the one who brought you into the world, with a hand on your shoulder.
G2Fotografo.8.easy: You stay still for a whole minute, your neck held in an iron clamp, while the photographer counts aloud. The portrait is ready two days later. There you are, stiff-backed and pale; and behind you, only a little lighter than the fog, is your parent, with a hand on your shoulder.
G2Fotografo.8.short: In your portrait, behind you, stands your parent, with a hand on your shoulder.

G2Fotografo.9.full: You recognise the hand before the face: the ink-stained fingers, the ring that went into the coffin. Mr Hartmann, when you point it out to him, becomes very serious and refuses to be paid.
G2Fotografo.9.easy: You know the hand before the face: the ink-stained fingers, the ring that went into the coffin. When you point it out, Mr Hartmann turns very serious and will not take your money.
G2Fotografo.9.short: You recognise the ring that went into the coffin. Hartmann will not take your money.

G2Fotografo.11.full: You overturn the table of plates, and the glass shatters on the gravel with a sound of little bells. The photographer does not react: he looks at you with infinite pity, the way one looks at a customer who has not understood.
G2Fotografo.11.easy: You overturn the table of plates, and the glass shatters on the gravel with a sound like little bells. The photographer does not react: he looks at you with endless pity, like a customer who has not understood.
G2Fotografo.11.short: You smash the plates. The photographer looks at you with pity, like a customer who has not understood.

G2Fotografo.12.full: Picking up the shards so as not to leave them for the children, you find one bigger than the rest, with a piece of portrait still intact: a shoulder, a hand, and a face you know from family photographs. The plate is dated three days ago. Nobody in your family has ever had a portrait taken here.
G2Fotografo.12.easy: Gathering the pieces so the children won't find them, you find one bigger than the rest, with part of a portrait still whole: a shoulder, a hand, and a face you know from family photographs. The plate is from three days ago. No one in your family has ever sat for a portrait here.
G2Fotografo.12.short: Among the shards is a face you know from family photos. The plate is from three days ago.

G2Fotografo.14.full: Mr Hartmann laughs, counts the coins and lets you into the tent. The trick is simple: the plate is exposed twice, once with the customer and once with the portrait of the dead person, which the family itself supplies without knowing it, by answering his kindly questions. A gauze veil in front of the lens does the rest.
G2Fotografo.14.easy: Mr Hartmann laughs, counts the coins and lets you into the tent. The trick is simple: the plate is exposed twice, once with the customer and once with the portrait of the dead person, which the family gives him without realising, by answering his kind questions. A gauze veil over the lens does the rest.
G2Fotografo.14.short: The trick is simple: the plate is exposed twice, once with the customer and once with a portrait of the dead.

G2Fotografo.15.full: Then, as he sees you out, he stops in front of a plate hung up to dry. "This one, though, no," he says quietly. "This one I didn't make." He will not let you look at it.
G2Fotografo.15.easy: Then, as he walks you out, he stops in front of a plate hung up to dry. "This one, though, no," he says quietly. "I didn't make this one." He will not let you look at it.
G2Fotografo.15.short: Then he points to a hanging plate: "I didn't make this one." He won't let you see it.

G2Chierichetto.2.full: After Mass, as you leave the church, a twelve-year-old boy runs after you with his surplice still on, sticking-out ears and the air of someone who has thought long before making up his mind. His name is Benedek, and he is Father Anzelm's altar boy: the one who yawns at every Mass for the dead.
G2Chierichetto.2.easy: After Mass, as you leave the church, a twelve-year-old boy runs after you with his surplice still on, ears sticking out and the look of someone who has thought hard before deciding. His name is Benedek, and he is Father Anzelm's altar boy: the one who yawns at every Mass for the dead.
G2Chierichetto.2.short: After Mass Benedek, Father Anzelm's twelve-year-old altar boy, runs after you.

G2Chierichetto.3.full: He drags you behind a pillar and tells you, all in one breath, that the sexton secretly copies the register of the dead every evening, and on Thursdays takes the copies to a gentleman with a black flower in his buttonhole. And that is not all: the sexton listens to confessions from the sacristy, through the grille. "The Circle knows everything about everyone," he says. "That's why the dead know so much at the séances." He is frightened, and it shows.
G2Chierichetto.3.easy: He pulls you behind a pillar and tells you, all in one breath, that the sexton secretly copies the register of the dead every evening, and on Thursdays takes the copies to a gentleman with a black flower in his buttonhole. And more: the sexton listens to confessions from the sacristy, through the grille. "The Circle knows everything about everyone," he says. "That's why the dead know so much at the séances." He is scared, and it shows.
G2Chierichetto.3.short: The sexton, he says, copies the register of the dead and listens to confessions for the Circle. "That's why the dead know so much at séances."

G2Chierichetto.6.full: You pay the sexton to report to you as well.

G2Chierichetto.7.full: You tell the boy to mind his own business.

G2Chierichetto.8.full: Father Anzelm dismisses the sexton that same day, without a word, with a wave of the hand worth more than an excommunication. In his place he takes the boy, who from that day serves Mass with his ears red with pride.
G2Chierichetto.8.easy: Father Anzelm dismisses the sexton that very day, without a word, with a wave of the hand worth more than an excommunication. In his place he takes the boy, who from then on serves Mass with his ears red with pride.
G2Chierichetto.8.short: Father Anzelm dismisses the sexton and takes the proud boy in his place.

G2Chierichetto.9.full: Benedek does not forget who listened to him. Every time he meets you he takes off his cap; and now and then he tells you, quietly, what he hears in the sacristy.
G2Chierichetto.9.easy: Benedek does not forget who listened to him. Every time he meets you he takes off his cap; and now and then he quietly tells you what he hears in the sacristy.
G2Chierichetto.9.short: Benedek does not forget: he always greets you, and tells you what he hears.

G2Chierichetto.10.full: Gain 1VP and move back 1 space on the {icon:Creepy_Icon} track.

G2Chierichetto.11.full: The sexton accepts your money as naturally as he accepts the Circle's. From that day on you know before anyone who has died, who is dying and who has confessed to what; and you arrive at grieving families with a word of comfort before the gravedigger does.
G2Chierichetto.11.easy: The sexton takes your money as easily as he takes the Circle's. From that day you know before anyone who has died, who is dying and who has confessed what; and you reach grieving families with a word of comfort before the gravedigger does.
G2Chierichetto.11.short: The sexton takes your money too. Now you reach grieving families before the gravedigger.

G2Chierichetto.12.full: Benedek watches you pass the sacristy door on Thursdays, with a face you will not forget. He has understood everything. He is twelve, and he has just learned how the world works.
G2Chierichetto.12.easy: Benedek sees you go by the sacristy door on Thursdays, with a face you will not forget. He has understood everything. He is twelve, and has just learned how the world works.
G2Chierichetto.12.short: Benedek sees you go by on Thursdays. He is twelve, and has just learned how the world works.

G2Chierichetto.14.full: You tell him that sacristy matters are none of your business, and that an altar boy who tells tales comes to a bad end. The boy blushes, lowers his head and goes back into the church without a word.
G2Chierichetto.14.easy: You tell him that sacristy business is none of yours, and that an altar boy who tells tales comes to a bad end. The boy goes red, lowers his head and goes back into the church without a word.
G2Chierichetto.14.short: You tell him to mind his own business. He goes back into the church without a word.

G2Chierichetto.15.full: The following Sunday, at Mass, he no longer yawns. He looks at you throughout the service, from the altar, with the eyes of a grown man.
G2Chierichetto.15.easy: The next Sunday, at Mass, he no longer yawns. He watches you all through the service, from the altar, with the eyes of a grown man.
G2Chierichetto.15.short: The next Sunday he no longer yawns. He watches you from the altar with a grown man's eyes.

G2Coprifuoco.2.full: Mayor Bódi has called an extraordinary session of the council. In the fog, he says, people go out at night to look for their dead, and do not always come back: three missing since September, one found at dawn in the cemetery, sitting on a grave that was not his family's, talking to himself. He proposes a curfew: nobody in the streets from dusk to dawn, until the fog lifts.
G2Coprifuoco.2.easy: Mayor Bódi has called a special meeting of the council. In the fog, he says, people go out at night to look for their dead, and do not always come back: three missing since September, one found at dawn in the cemetery, sitting on a grave that was not his family's, talking to himself. He proposes a curfew: no one in the streets from dusk to dawn, until the fog lifts.
G2Coprifuoco.2.short: In the fog people go out to look for their dead, and do not always come back. The Mayor proposes a curfew.

G2Coprifuoco.3.full: The families of the Circle protest: the dead, they say, only speak at night. The priest approves. The Mayor looks towards the family from the estate, the way one looks at the needle of a scale.
G2Coprifuoco.3.easy: The Circle's families protest: the dead, they say, only speak at night. The priest approves. The Mayor looks at the family from the estate, the way one watches the needle of a scale.
G2Coprifuoco.3.short: The Circle protests, the priest approves. The Mayor looks at you: it is your call.

G2Coprifuoco.6.full: You oppose it: the living have the right to look for their dead.

G2Coprifuoco.7.full: The curfew passes by one vote. From that evening the watchmen go round with lanterns and a hand bell, and anyone found in the street spends the night at the town hall. The streets of {0}, at night, are empty; but the watchmen say that the bell sometimes rings by itself, and that someone in the fog answers.
G2Coprifuoco.7.easy: The curfew passes by one vote. From that evening the watchmen go round with lanterns and a hand bell, and anyone found in the street spends the night at the town hall. At night the streets of {0} are empty; but the watchmen say that the bell sometimes rings on its own, and that someone in the fog answers.
G2Coprifuoco.7.short: The curfew passes. The streets are empty at night, but the watchmen's bell sometimes rings on its own.

G2Coprifuoco.9.full: The curfew does not pass. That same evening the streets fill with lanterns: widows, mothers, old people going to the cemetery in procession, singing softly. Some stop you to thank you. A woman takes your hand and tells you that tonight, at last, she will be able to talk to her son.
G2Coprifuoco.9.easy: The curfew does not pass. That very evening the streets fill with lanterns: widows, mothers, old people walking to the cemetery in procession, singing softly. Some stop to thank you. A woman takes your hand and tells you that tonight, at last, she will be able to talk to her son.
G2Coprifuoco.9.short: The curfew fails. The streets fill with lanterns, and a mother thanks you: tonight she will talk to her son.

G2Casa.2.full: At the Builder's Office the foreman Szabó is waiting for you, an honest, frightened man. A year ago he built a house for a newly married couple, at the end of the mill road: new bricks, new beams, nothing old. Since the fog came down, the walls knock. The couple are sleeping at the mother-in-law's.
G2Casa.2.easy: At the Builder's Office the foreman Szabó is waiting for you, an honest and frightened man. A year ago he built a house for a young married couple, at the end of the mill road: new bricks, new beams, nothing old. Since the fog came, the walls knock. The couple are sleeping at the mother-in-law's.
G2Casa.2.short: The foreman Szabó built a new house. Since the fog came, its walls knock.

G2Casa.3.full: Jóska the smith swears he never laid a hand on it, and Szabó believes him: he built every wall himself, and knows there is nothing inside. "You," he says, "are the only ones who can tell me whether I built a house or a door."
G2Casa.3.easy: Jóska the smith swears he never touched it, and Szabó believes him: he built every wall himself, and knows there is nothing inside them. "You," he says, "are the only ones who can tell me whether I built a house or a door."
G2Casa.3.short: Jóska had nothing to do with it. "You tell me whether I built a house or a door," says Szabó.

G2Casa.5.full: You spend a night in the house.

G2Casa.6.full: You have the wall that knocks loudest knocked down.

G2Casa.7.full: You get paid for a séance that will "cleanse" the house.

G2Casa.8.full: You spend the night on a chair, in the middle of the empty bedroom, with a candle and the Journal. At midnight the knocking begins, in the north wall, the one facing the estate. You count the knocks. You write them down. At dawn you have three pages of letters that make no words, but that, read backwards, spell the name of the street where you were born.
G2Casa.8.easy: You spend the night on a chair in the middle of the empty bedroom, with a candle and the Journal. At midnight the knocking starts, in the north wall, the one facing the estate. You count the knocks. You write them down. At dawn you have three pages of letters that make no words, but that, read backwards, spell the name of the street where you were born.
G2Casa.8.short: You spend the night there writing down the knocks. Read backwards, they spell the street where you were born.

G2Casa.10.full: The workmen knock down the wall in a morning. Inside there is nothing: bricks, mortar, a mouse's nest. The knocking stops. The couple go home, the foreman thanks you with tears in his eyes. Only Jóska the smith, looking at the rubble, makes a face: among the bricks there is a child's shoe, small, wet, which nobody put there.
G2Casa.10.easy: The workmen knock down the wall in one morning. There is nothing inside: bricks, mortar, a mouse's nest. The knocking stops. The couple go home, and the foreman thanks you with tears in his eyes. Only Jóska the smith, looking at the rubble, pulls a face: among the bricks is a child's shoe, small and wet, that no one put there.
G2Casa.10.short: The wall comes down, and the knocking stops. But among the bricks is a child's wet shoe.

G2Casa.12.full: You hold a séance by the book, like Madame's: candles, joined hands, a throat voice, a tap of a pedal hidden under the rug. You announce that the spirit has gone in peace. The couple weep with gratitude and pay you well. The knocking, for a week, really stops. Then it starts again, louder; and one knock, they tell you, is shaped like a laugh.
G2Casa.12.easy: You hold a perfect séance, just like Madame's: candles, joined hands, a throat voice, a pedal hidden under the rug. You announce that the spirit has gone in peace. The couple cry with gratitude and pay you well. For a week the knocking really stops. Then it starts again, louder; and one knock, they tell you, sounds like a laugh.
G2Casa.12.short: You hold a fake séance and are paid well. The knocking stops for a week, then returns louder, like laughter.

G2Pub.3.full: In the little room at the back of the Pub, behind a velvet curtain, Madame Vámos receives anyone who buys the landlord a drink and asks no questions.
G2Pub.3.easy: In the small room at the back of the Pub, behind a velvet curtain, Madame Vámos sees anyone who buys the landlord a drink and asks no questions.
G2Pub.3.short: At the back of the Pub, Madame Vámos receives those who ask no questions.

G2Pub.4.full: Madame Vámos is gone, but her chair, in the little room at the back of the Pub, is still in its place. Whoever sits down before it, hands on the little table, hears her voice.
G2Pub.4.easy: Madame Vámos is gone, but her chair is still in the small room at the back of the Pub. Whoever sits in front of it, with their hands on the little table, hears her voice.
G2Pub.4.short: Madame is gone, but whoever sits before her chair still hears her voice.

G2Pub.5.full: In the little room at the back of the Pub a pale girl, who says she was a pupil of the woman in the wagon, holds séances for a few coins.
G2Pub.5.easy: In the small room at the back of the Pub a pale girl, who says she studied with the woman in the wagon, holds séances for a little money.
G2Pub.5.short: At the back of the Pub, a pupil of the woman in the wagon holds séances for a few coins.

G2Pub.6.full: The medium's voice turns hoarse and masculine: it is a miller who died of cholera, she says, who trusted banks even less than priests. He describes a loose brick behind the stove of an abandoned mill. You go there the next day, the fog up to your knees. The brick is there. Behind it is a tin box full of coins, and no one, as far as you know, will ever come to claim it.
G2Pub.6.easy: The medium's voice becomes rough, like a man's: it is a miller who died of cholera, she says, who trusted banks even less than priests. He describes a loose brick behind the stove of an abandoned mill. You go there the next day, with fog up to your knees. The brick is there. Behind it is a tin box full of coins, and no one, as far as you know, will ever come to take it.
G2Pub.6.short: A miller who died of cholera speaks and points you to a loose brick in an abandoned mill. Behind it is a box of coins no one will claim.

G2Pub.8.full: The medium's hands grip yours for a long time. Then a name comes: that of the person in town who fears you most and spreads rumours about you. It is a name you know. The next day you call on them with a basket of fruit and a smile. The rumours, mysteriously, die away.
G2Pub.8.easy: The medium holds your hands for a long time. Then she says a name: that of the person in town who is most afraid of you and says bad things about you. You know that name. The next day you visit them with a basket of fruit and a smile. The rumours, strangely, stop.
G2Pub.8.short: The medium names the one spreading rumours about you. A visit with a basket of fruit, and the rumours die away.

G2Pub.10.full: In the middle of a sentence the medium's voice changes: it becomes lower, slower, with an accent you have only heard in family stories. It is Grandfather. He calls you by name, your name, and tells you that in the fog the veil is as thin as wet paper, and that a single finger would be enough to pierce it. Then the candle goes out, and the voice falls silent.
G2Pub.10.easy: In the middle of a sentence the medium's voice changes: it gets lower and slower, with an accent you have only heard in family stories. It is Grandfather. He calls you by name and tells you that in the fog the veil is as thin as wet paper: one finger would be enough to make a hole in it. Then the candle goes out, and the voice is silent.
G2Pub.10.short: The medium's voice becomes Grandfather's: "In the fog the veil is as thin as wet paper. One finger could pierce it." Then the candle goes out.

G2Pub.13.full: You leave an offering on the little table.

G2Pub.14.full: You look under the table, when nobody is watching.

G2Pub.15.full: You leave a coin on the velvet. The medium does not look at it; she holds your hand and whispers a name, that of a village family who have just lost someone and who, she says, need you more than you need the dead. You go the next day. She is right.
G2Pub.15.easy: You leave a coin on the velvet. The medium does not look at it; she holds your hand and whispers a name, that of a village family who have just lost someone and who, she says, need you more than you need the dead. You go the next day. She is right.
G2Pub.15.short: The medium whispers the name of a grieving family who need you. You go. She is right.

G2Pub.17.full: While the medium shows another client out, you bend down under the table. The pedal is there, as in the stories of those who used to visit the caravan years ago. But it is covered in dust, and the dust has not been touched for months.
G2Pub.17.easy: While the medium shows another client out, you bend down under the table. The pedal is there, just as in the stories of those who visited the caravan long ago. But it is covered in dust, and the dust has not been touched for months.
G2Pub.17.short: Under the table is the pedal. But it is dusty, and no one has used it for months.

G2Pub.18.full: While nobody is watching, you bend down under the table. No pedals, no threads, no holes in the floorboards: only old wood and a child's shoe, small, wet, which nobody knows where it came from.
G2Pub.18.easy: While no one is looking, you bend down under the table. No pedals, no threads, no holes in the floor: only old wood and a child's shoe, small and wet, that no one knows anything about.
G2Pub.18.short: Under the table there are no tricks: only a child's wet shoe.

G2Asilo.2.full: The Asylum Program is an old whitewashed barracks, with barred windows and an iron cross on the gate. Father Anzelm, stooped now, runs it with the help of two nuns and an enormous orderly who never speaks. The fog has brought the "possessed" here: people who speak with voices not their own, who write in languages they never studied, who knock on the walls for hours.
G2Asilo.2.easy: The Asylum Program is an old barracks painted white, with bars on the windows and an iron cross on the gate. Father Anzelm, bent with age now, runs it with two nuns and a huge orderly who never speaks. The fog has brought the "possessed" here: people who speak with voices not their own, who write in languages they never learned, who knock on the walls for hours.
G2Asilo.2.short: At the Asylum Program, Father Anzelm treats the fog's "possessed": people who speak in others' voices and knock on the walls for hours.

G2Asilo.3.full: The cure is harsh: icy baths, prayers, leather straps, silence. In some way it does you good to see how thin the line is between them and you. But the man in cell number seven, when you pass, stops knocking and greets you by your name, in your grandfather's voice.
G2Asilo.3.easy: The cure is hard: freezing baths, prayers, leather straps, silence. In a way it does you good to see how small the difference is between them and you. But the man in cell number seven, when you walk past, stops knocking and says hello using your name, and your grandfather's voice.
G2Asilo.3.short: The cure is harsh, and it does you good. But the man in cell seven greets you by name, in your grandfather's voice.

G2Asilo.4.full: Move back 2 spaces on the {icon:Insanity_Icon} track and gain 1 {icon:Creepy_Icon}.

G2GrandeSeduta.3.full: For All Saints' night Madame Vámos summons the whole village to the Temple of the Circle, or to what has been built of it. Two hundred come, with lanterns, through the fog. In the middle of the hall stands a round table, with a chair for each heir of the estate and two more: one for Madame, one empty.
G2GrandeSeduta.3.easy: For All Saints' night Madame Vámos invites the whole village to the Temple of the Circle, or to the part of it that has been built. Two hundred people come, with lanterns, through the fog. In the middle of the hall there is a round table, with a chair for each heir of the estate and two more chairs: one for Madame and one empty.
G2GrandeSeduta.3.short: On All Saints' night two hundred people cross the fog to the Temple. At the table, a chair for each heir, one for Madame, and one empty.

G2GrandeSeduta.4.full: Madame announces that tonight, with the help of the founder's blood, she will try to summon him: the man who first wrote that veils can be lifted. The minutes are taken by {0}, at the medium's wish, "so that they are written by a hand of the family".
G2GrandeSeduta.4.easy: Madame says that tonight, with the help of the founder's blood, she will try to call him: the man who first wrote that veils can be lifted. {0} writes the record, because the medium wants it: "so it is written by a hand of the family".
G2GrandeSeduta.4.short: Madame will try to summon the founder, with the help of his blood. {0} takes the minutes, "a hand of the family".

G2GrandeSeduta.5.full: Without a medium, the family manages on its own. On All Saints' night the heirs sit around the old table in the laboratory, the one Grandfather used for his experiments in magnetism, with the Journal open at its last page and an empty chair at the head of the table. The minutes are taken by {0}.
G2GrandeSeduta.5.easy: There is no medium, so the family does it alone. On All Saints' night the heirs sit around the old table in the laboratory, the one Grandfather used for his experiments with magnetism. The Journal is open at the last page and there is an empty chair at the head of the table. {0} writes the record.
G2GrandeSeduta.5.short: Without a medium, the heirs sit alone around the old laboratory table, an empty chair at its head. {0} takes the minutes.

G2GrandeSeduta.6.full: Outside, the fog presses against the windows. None of them has ever conducted a séance; all of them, however, have read enough to know how it is done. That, more than anything else, is what is frightening.
G2GrandeSeduta.6.easy: Outside, the fog presses against the windows. None of them has ever led a séance, but they have all read enough to know how to do it. That is exactly what is most frightening.
G2GrandeSeduta.6.short: None of them has ever led a séance, but all of them know how. That is what is frightening.

G2GrandeSeduta.7.full: Hartmann the photographer, invited by the family, has set up his camera in a corner, with the plate ready and the magnesium in its dish.
G2GrandeSeduta.7.easy: Hartmann the photographer, invited by the family, has set up his camera in a corner, the plate ready and the magnesium in its dish.
G2GrandeSeduta.7.short: In a corner Hartmann the photographer stands ready.

G2GrandeSeduta.8.full: Hartmann the photographer, despite the broken plates, has turned up with a new camera, and nobody has had the courage to send him away.
G2GrandeSeduta.8.easy: Hartmann the photographer, despite the broken plates, has come with a new camera, and no one has dared send him away.
G2GrandeSeduta.8.short: Hartmann the photographer has come anyway, with a new camera.

G2GrandeSeduta.9.full: For one night, curfew or not, the village streets are full of lanterns: anyone who wishes crosses the fog to come and see.
G2GrandeSeduta.9.easy: For one night, curfew or no curfew, the village streets are full of lanterns: anyone who wants to crosses the fog to come and see.
G2GrandeSeduta.9.short: For one night the streets are full of lanterns: everyone wants to see.

G2GrandeSeduta.10.full: At the door, with his surplice under his coat and a bucket of holy water, stands Benedek the altar boy, sent by Father Anzelm "to watch and to remember".
G2GrandeSeduta.10.easy: At the door, his surplice under his coat and a bucket of holy water in his hand, stands Benedek the altar boy, sent by Father Anzelm "to watch and to remember".
G2GrandeSeduta.10.short: At the door stands Benedek, sent by Father Anzelm "to watch and to remember".

G2GrandeSeduta.11.full: At midnight the candle flame in the middle of the table bends towards the empty chair, as if in a breath of air. It is time to decide.
G2GrandeSeduta.11.easy: At midnight the candle flame, in the middle of the table, bends towards the empty chair, as if blown by a breath of air. It is time to decide.
G2GrandeSeduta.11.short: At midnight the flame bends towards the empty chair. It is time to decide.

G2GrandeSedutaVoto.4.full: NAY: you break off the séance.

G2Ectoplasma.2.full: Madame Vámos closes her eyes and stiffens in her chair. Her lips part, and from her mouth a white, luminous substance begins to emerge, slowly, like a smoke with weight. It stretches across the table towards the empty chair and takes the shape of a hand. Then of an arm. Someone screams. The light becomes blinding.
G2Ectoplasma.2.easy: Madame Vámos closes her eyes and goes stiff in her chair. She opens her lips, and slowly a white, glowing substance begins to come out of her mouth, like heavy smoke. It stretches across the table towards the empty chair and takes the shape of a hand. Then an arm. Someone screams. The light becomes very bright.
G2Ectoplasma.2.short: A white, glowing substance pours from Madame's mouth, stretches towards the empty chair and takes the shape of a hand. The light blinds everyone.

G2Ectoplasma.3.full: When the dark returns, there is only her black shawl on Madame's chair. Of her body, no trace. On the table remains a pool of white substance, still warm, which someone, with a trembling hand, gathers into a vial.
G2Ectoplasma.3.easy: When the dark comes back, there is only her black shawl on Madame's chair. Her body is gone. On the table there is a pool of white substance, still warm, and someone, with a shaking hand, puts it into a vial.
G2Ectoplasma.3.short: In the dark, only her shawl is left on Madame's chair. Someone gathers the white substance on the table into a vial.

G2Ectoplasma.4.full: Madame Vámos throws her head back. From her mouth comes a white, stringy substance that gathers on the table in a small, glowing pool. The empty chair creaks, as if someone had just sat down in it. Then Madame coughs, wipes her lips with a handkerchief and says, in her usual voice: "He was here."
G2Ectoplasma.4.easy: Madame Vámos tips her head back. From her mouth comes a white, stringy substance that makes a small glowing pool on the table. The empty chair creaks, as if someone had just sat down. Then Madame coughs, wipes her lips with a handkerchief and says, in her normal voice: "He was here."
G2Ectoplasma.4.short: A white, glowing substance flows from Madame's mouth; the empty chair creaks. Then Madame wipes her lips: "He was here."

G2Ectoplasma.5.full: The doctor, the next day, will say it was gauze soaked in phosphorus. But the substance someone gathers into a vial still glows, months later.
G2Ectoplasma.5.easy: The next day the doctor will say it was gauze soaked in phosphorus. But the substance someone put in a vial is still glowing, months later.
G2Ectoplasma.5.short: Gauze and phosphorus, the doctor will say. But the vial still glows months later.

G2Ectoplasma.6.full: At midnight the youngest person at the table begins to speak in a voice that is not their own: low, slow, impatient. It utters three words in a dead language, then coughs, and from their mouth comes a white, stringy substance that glows in the dark.
G2Ectoplasma.6.easy: At midnight the youngest person at the table starts to speak with a voice that is not their own: low, slow, impatient. It says three words in an ancient language, then coughs, and a white, stringy substance that glows in the dark comes out of their mouth.
G2Ectoplasma.6.short: At midnight the youngest speaks in a voice not their own, then coughs up a white substance that glows in the dark.

G2Ectoplasma.7.full: In the morning no one remembers who fetched a vial from the laboratory to gather it. But the vial is full.
G2Ectoplasma.7.easy: In the morning no one remembers who took a vial from the laboratory to collect it. But the vial is full.
G2Ectoplasma.7.short: No one remembers who gathered it. But the vial is full.

G2Ectoplasma.8.full: Whoever has the highest {icon:Insanity_Icon} takes the vial (in case of a tie, the Start Player chooses among those tied).

G2Fiala.2.full: **{0}** takes the **Vial token** from the **The Cost of Disease** Scenario Box and keeps it in front of them until the end of the game.

G2SedutaInterrotta.2.full: Someone leaps up and throws open the shutters. The candle goes out; the empty chair tips over by itself, with a thud. For a long moment no one breathes.
G2SedutaInterrotta.2.easy: Someone suddenly stands up and opens the shutters. The candle goes out. The empty chair falls over by itself, with a thud. For a long moment no one breathes.
G2SedutaInterrotta.2.short: Someone throws open the shutters. The candle goes out and the empty chair falls by itself.

G2SedutaInterrotta.3.full: Then, outside, the fog thins a little, and for the first time in months the moon can be seen. Whatever was waiting on the other side of the table has gone. But it has gone away angry, and all winter long, at the estate, the doors slam by themselves.
G2SedutaInterrotta.3.easy: Then, outside, the fog gets a little thinner, and for the first time in months you can see the moon. Whatever was waiting on the other side of the table has gone. But it has gone away angry, and all winter, at the estate, the doors slam by themselves.
G2SedutaInterrotta.3.short: The fog thins and the moon returns. Whatever was waiting has gone, but angry: all winter the doors slam by themselves.

G2Segreti.2.full: A few weeks after the séance, Madame Vámos sends each heir a black-edged card. She does not have much time left, she writes; or perhaps she has too much. In any case the moment has come to leave someone her most precious secret: the way not to die entirely.
G2Segreti.2.easy: A few weeks after the séance, Madame Vámos sends each heir a card with a black border. She writes that she does not have much time left, or perhaps she has too much. Anyway, the moment has come to leave someone her most precious secret: the way not to die completely.
G2Segreti.2.short: Madame Vámos writes to the heirs: it is time to leave someone her most precious secret, the way not to die entirely.

G2Segreti.3.full: She will sell it to one person only: whoever can show they care for it most. "My spiritual children," she adds at the bottom of the card, "will understand that even eternity has a price."
G2Segreti.3.easy: She will sell it to only one person: whoever shows they want it most. "My spiritual children," she writes at the end of the card, "will understand that even eternity costs something."
G2Segreti.3.short: She will sell it to whoever wants it most: "even eternity has a price".

G2Segreti.4.full: Each player secretly takes in hand the money they wish to offer. When everyone is ready, reveal your offers together. Whoever offers the most pays and takes an **Immortality card**; the others take back their money.

G2SegretiEsito.2.full: Whoever offered the most draws an **Immortality card** at random from the **The Cost of Disease** Scenario Box. The printed text applies exactly as written.

G2R3.29.easy: Mayor Bódi, son of the man who was on the council in 1856, is ill and is looking for someone to take his place in politics.
