G3Conto.4.easy: And for fifty years, on the second day of every month, someone from your family has come to collect it. "Admirably regular," says the manager, without irony. "Like a pension."
G3Conto.4.short: And for fifty years your family has collected it. "Like a pension," says the manager.

G3Conto.5.full: After your family refused it, the sender stopped asking for it to be returned. The money has piled up in a suspense account, with interest, for half a century. The manager shows you the balance, and does so with a certain reverence.
G3Conto.5.easy: After your family refused it, the sender stopped asking for it to be sent back. The money has piled up in a separate account, with interest, for half a century. The manager shows you the balance with a certain reverence.
G3Conto.5.short: The money your family refused has piled up for half a century. The manager shows it to you with reverence.

G3Conto.6.full: Beside each deposit there is the same black carnation drawn in ink, and the same name, *O. Garai*, with the same pressure of the pen, from 1828 to this morning. The president of the Circle of the Last Hour, the manager tells you, lowering his voice, has that name.
G3Conto.6.easy: Beside each deposit is the same black carnation drawn in ink, and the same name, *O. Garai*, with the same pressure of the pen, from 1828 to this morning. The president of the Circle of the Last Hour, the manager tells you quietly, has that name.
G3Conto.6.short: Every deposit, from 1828 to today, is signed *O. Garai*. That is the name of the Circle's president.

G3Conto.9.full: You have the account closed, for ever.

G3Conto.10.full: You follow the money: you ask where the rest ends up.

G3Conto.11.full: The manager counts the money in a separate room, with two clerks and an armoured door. You leave with a full leather bag and the feeling, which you cannot shake off, that someone has just paid you for something. For what, you will find out at the end.
G3Conto.11.easy: The manager counts the money in a separate room, with two clerks and a steel door. You leave with a full leather bag and the feeling, which you cannot shake, that someone has just paid you for something. For what, you will learn at the end.
G3Conto.11.short: You leave with a bag full of money, and the feeling that someone has paid you for something.

G3Conto.13.full: You sign the closure of the account. The manager hesitates, then rules a line under the last figure, and writes *closed* in fine copperplate. The pen spits a drop of ink onto the page, right above the word.
G3Conto.13.easy: You sign to close the account. The manager hesitates, then rules a line under the last figure and writes *closed* in his best hand. The pen spits a drop of ink onto the page, right on top of the word.
G3Conto.13.short: You close the account. The manager writes *closed*, and the pen spits a drop of ink onto the word.

G3Conto.14.full: On the first of the following month, a deposit arrives at the National Bank from Budapest, made out to an account that no longer exists. The bank returns it. Another arrives, the next day. Then another.
G3Conto.14.easy: On the first of the next month, a deposit arrives at the National Bank from Budapest for an account that no longer exists. The bank sends it back. Another comes the next day. Then another.
G3Conto.14.short: The next month a deposit arrives for the closed account. Then another, and another.

G3Conto.16.full: The manager, flattered to be taken seriously, shows you the flows: a Budapest company, the same one that bought the new shops on the square; then the Circle's funeral parlour; then a smith, a pharmacist, a photographer, a retired sexton. Fifty years of wages. These are not the expenses of a spiritualist society: they are the expenses of a theatre.
G3Conto.16.easy: The manager, pleased to be taken seriously, shows you where the money goes: a Budapest company, the same one that bought the new shops on the square; then the Circle's funeral parlour; then a smith, a pharmacist, a photographer, a retired sexton. Fifty years of wages. These are not a spiritualist society's expenses: they are a theatre's.
G3Conto.16.short: The Circle's money pays a smith, a pharmacist, a photographer, a sexton. It is not a spiritualist society: it is a theatre.

G3Conto.17.full: You copy everything into a notebook. As you leave, you notice that a page of the ledger, the one for 1848, has been torn out. The manager swears it was there yesterday.
G3Conto.17.easy: You copy it all into a notebook. As you leave, you notice that a page of the ledger, the one for 1848, has been torn out. The manager swears it was there yesterday.
G3Conto.17.short: You copy it all. But the page for 1848 has been torn out. The manager swears it was there yesterday.

G3Margini.2.full: At the Public Library, in the rare books room, the librarian hands you, wearing gloves, a little octavo volume bound in board: *Des tables parlantes et des esprits frappeurs*, Paris, 1827. It comes, she says, from the library of your family's founder, sold at auction to pay his debts in 1857. It is the booklet someone saw on Father's shelf on the first night.
G3Margini.2.easy: At the Public Library, in the rare books room, the librarian hands you, wearing gloves, a small book bound in card: *Des tables parlantes et des esprits frappeurs*, Paris, 1827. It comes, she says, from the library of your family's founder, sold at auction to pay debts in 1857. It is the booklet someone saw on Father's shelf on the first night.
G3Margini.2.short: The library has the French booklet on talking tables, the one on the founder's shelf on the first night.

G3Margini.3.full: The margins are thick with notes, in two hands. One is the Journal's. The other is small, elegant, feminine. The two hands answer each other, correct each other, tease each other. At the bottom of the last page, under the date 1828, are three names one beneath the other, as in a deed: the founder's, *Eszter Vámos* and *O. Garai*. And above them, underlined: *Circle of the Last Hour*.
G3Margini.3.easy: The margins are full of notes, in two hands. One is the Journal's. The other is small, elegant, a woman's. The two hands answer each other, correct each other, tease each other. At the bottom of the last page, under the date 1828, are three names one under another, as in a contract: the founder's, *Eszter Vámos* and *O. Garai*. And above them, underlined: *Circle of the Last Hour*.
G3Margini.3.short: On the last page, under the date 1828, are three names: the founder, *Eszter Vámos* and *O. Garai*. And above them: *Circle of the Last Hour*.

G3Margini.5.full: You tear out the last page, for the family's good name.

G3Margini.6.full: You take the booklet to Dr Lukács.

G3Margini.7.full: You put it back, and speak of it to nobody.

G3Margini.8.full: You wait for the librarian to turn away, and the page comes away with a noise that seems deafening to you. At home you burn it in the stove. The paper curls, blackens, and for a moment, before turning to ash, the three names glow red, one beneath the other.
G3Margini.8.easy: You wait for the librarian to turn away, and the page tears off with a sound that seems deafening to you. At home you burn it in the stove. The paper curls and blackens, and for a moment, before it turns to ash, the three names glow red, one under another.
G3Margini.8.short: You tear out the page and burn it. Before turning to ash, the three names glow red.

G3Margini.9.full: The founder of your family, then, was not a correspondent of the Circle. He founded it. And the knocking on the first night, perhaps, was a surprise to nobody, except his children.
G3Margini.9.easy: So your family's founder was not just a correspondent of the Circle. He founded it. And the knocking on the first night, perhaps, surprised no one but his children.
G3Margini.9.short: The founder did not just write to the Circle: he founded it. Perhaps the first night's knocking surprised only his children.

G3Margini.11.full: Dr Lukács reads the margins twice, with a magnifying glass, then takes off his spectacles and rubs his eyes. "Three friends," he says, "a physician, an actress and a businessman, who in 1828 invent a society for talking to the dead. It's the proof I've been looking for for forty years." Then he puts his spectacles back on. "Or the proof that someone, in 1828, already knew what was going to happen."
G3Margini.11.easy: Dr Lukács reads the margins twice, with a magnifying glass, then takes off his glasses and rubs his eyes. "Three friends," he says, "a doctor, an actress and a businessman, who in 1828 invent a society for talking to the dead. It's the proof I've been looking for for forty years." Then he puts his glasses back on. "Or the proof that someone, in 1828, already knew what would happen."
G3Margini.11.short: "Three friends who in 1828 invent a society for talking to the dead," says Lukács. "It's the proof I wanted. Or proof that they already knew what would happen."

G3Margini.13.full: You put the booklet back in its box and return it to the librarian with a smile. You speak of it to nobody: not the family, not Dr Lukács, not the Circle. But at night, at the estate, you catch yourself knocking softly on the wall of your room, once, as one asks permission; and from the other side someone answers, with a patience that seems satisfied.
G3Margini.13.easy: You put the booklet back in its box and return it to the librarian with a smile. You tell no one: not the family, not Dr Lukács, not the Circle. But at night, at the estate, you find yourself knocking softly on your bedroom wall, once, as if asking permission; and from the other side someone answers, with a patience that sounds satisfied.
G3Margini.13.short: You tell no one. But at night you find yourself knocking softly on the wall; and someone answers, satisfied.

G3Cilindro.2.full: At the Laborer's Union, a young, thin electrician approaches you with the air of someone selling stolen goods. He worked on the electrical installation of the Circle's Temple, he says, and during a séance he hid a phonograph behind a curtain, for a bet with his mates. The wax cylinder is in a hatbox, wrapped in cotton wool.
G3Cilindro.2.easy: At the Laborer's Union a thin young electrician comes up to you like someone selling stolen goods. He worked on the wiring of the Circle's Temple, he says, and during a séance he hid a phonograph behind a curtain, for a bet with his mates. The wax cylinder is in a hatbox, wrapped in cotton wool.
G3Cilindro.2.short: An electrician secretly recorded a Circle séance, on a wax cylinder.

G3Cilindro.3.full: "The voices are on it," he whispers. "The dead ones. I didn't want to listen to it again. Nor did my mates." He wants to get rid of it, and wants the family from the estate to take it: you, he says, know what to do with it.
G3Cilindro.3.easy: "The voices are on it," he whispers. "The dead ones. I didn't want to hear it again. Nor did the others." He wants to be rid of it, and wants the family from the estate to have it: you, he says, will know what to do with it.
G3Cilindro.3.short: "The voices of the dead are on it. You take it: you'll know what to do with it."

G3Cilindro.5.full: You listen to it, alone, at night.

G3Cilindro.6.full: You take it to Dr Lukács.

G3Cilindro.7.full: You break it without listening to it.

G3Cilindro.8.full: The needle scratches, hisses, and then you hear voices in a room, coughing, a creaking table. Then one voice closer than the others, hoarse, as if recorded through a brass tube. It says your family's name, and then yours, clearly, twice. On the cylinder's label there is a date: two years before you came to town.
G3Cilindro.8.easy: The needle scratches and hisses, and then you hear voices in a room, coughs, a creaking table. Then one voice closer than the rest, hoarse, as if recorded through a brass tube. It says your family's name, and then yours, clearly, twice. On the cylinder's label is a date: two years before you came to town.
G3Cilindro.8.short: A hoarse voice says your name, twice. But the cylinder dates from two years before you came to town.

G3Cilindro.10.full: Dr Lukács listens to the cylinder three times, the last slowing the phonograph with his finger. At the right speed, the voice of the "dead man" is Mr Garai's, with a carnation in his mouth, one would say, and a brass tube in front of his lips. The doctor notes everything down, and thanks you. Then he adds, more quietly, that there is another voice, at the end of the recording, which he cannot recognise, and which he did not want to slow down.
G3Cilindro.10.easy: Dr Lukács listens to the cylinder three times, the last time slowing the phonograph with his finger. At the right speed, the "dead man's" voice is Mr Garai's, with a carnation in his mouth, one might say, and a brass tube at his lips. The doctor writes it all down and thanks you. Then he adds, more quietly, that there is another voice, at the end of the recording, which he cannot place, and which he did not want to slow down.
G3Cilindro.10.short: Slowed down, the "dead man's" voice is Garai's. But at the end is another voice, which Lukács cannot place.

G3Cilindro.12.full: The cylinder breaks into three pieces on the cobbles, like a biscuit. The electrician looks at you with enormous relief, thanks you twice and leaves almost at a run. That evening, at the café in the square, the phonograph plays by itself, for a minute, a song nobody put on.
G3Cilindro.12.easy: The cylinder breaks into three on the cobbles, like a biscuit. The electrician looks hugely relieved, thanks you twice and leaves almost at a run. That evening, at the café on the square, the phonograph plays by itself, for a minute, a song no one put on.
G3Cilindro.12.short: You break the cylinder. That evening the café phonograph plays a song by itself.

G3Censimento.2.full: It is the census year, and at the Town Hall the clerk responsible for the hill district, a young man with spectacles and inky fingers, stops you in the corridor with the estate's form in his hand. He has a problem, he says, and does not know how to write it down.
G3Censimento.2.easy: It is census year, and at the Town Hall the clerk for the hill district, a young man with glasses and inky fingers, stops you in the corridor with the estate's form in his hand. He has a problem, he says, and does not know how to write it down.
G3Censimento.2.short: It is census year. The clerk stops you with the estate's form: he has a problem.

G3Censimento.3.full: On the evening of his visit, when he came to count the inhabitants, he saw the family at table, in the dining room, through the window. He counted one person per chair, as one does. There were eleven chairs. On the form, however, the family declared only the living; and he would like to know who the others were, for completeness.
G3Censimento.3.easy: On the evening of his visit, when he came to count the residents, he saw the family at table in the dining room, through the window. He counted one person per chair, as one does. There were eleven chairs. On the form, however, the family listed only the living; and he would like to know who the others were, to be thorough.
G3Censimento.3.short: Through the window he counted eleven people at table. The form lists only the living. Who were the others?

G3Censimento.5.full: You sign the form with the clerk's number: eleven.

G3Censimento.6.full: You have the number corrected: the living only.

G3Censimento.7.full: You ask him to describe the others to you.

G3Censimento.8.full: You sign. The form goes to Budapest with the others, and the estate, in the Kingdom's statistics, appears as the most populous house in the province. A few months later a letter arrives from the central office, asking for the ages of "seven residents not entered in the register". Nobody answers. The letter, on the hall table, turns yellow overnight.
G3Censimento.8.easy: You sign. The form goes to Budapest with the others, and the estate appears in the Kingdom's statistics as the most crowded house in the province. A few months later a letter comes from the central office, asking for the ages of "seven residents not on the register". No one answers. The letter, on the hall table, turns yellow overnight.
G3Censimento.8.short: You sign "eleven". Budapest asks for the ages of "seven unregistered residents". No one answers.

G3Censimento.10.full: The clerk corrects the number with a sigh of relief. He thanks you: he thought he was going mad. As you leave the town hall you turn towards the hill, and for a moment you seem to see, at the dining-room windows, figures moving away, offended, like guests who have been told dinner is over.
G3Censimento.10.easy: The clerk corrects the number with a sigh of relief. He thanks you: he thought he was going mad. As you leave the town hall you look towards the hill, and for a moment you seem to see, at the dining-room windows, figures moving away, offended, like guests told that dinner is over.
G3Censimento.10.short: You have the number corrected. At your windows you seem to see figures leaving, offended.

G3Censimento.12.full: The clerk describes them with a bookkeeper's precision: an elderly gentleman at the head of the table, with a notebook; a lady with a black shawl; two people who look very much like the ones who brought you into the world; an old couple holding hands; and a child with wet clothes, playing with the crumbs. "They were all eating," he says. "That's what struck me. Nobody touched their plate, but they were all eating."
G3Censimento.12.easy: The clerk describes them with a bookkeeper's precision: an old gentleman at the head of the table, with a notebook; a lady with a black shawl; two people who look very like your parents; an old couple holding hands; and a child in wet clothes, playing with the crumbs. "They were all eating," he says. "That's what struck me. No one touched their plate, but they were all eating."
G3Censimento.12.short: An old man with a notebook, a lady in a black shawl, your parents, a wet child. "No one touched their plate, but they were all eating."

G3Facciate.3.full: **NEW SHOPS, FEW CUSTOMERS.** In the last month several new shops have opened in {0}, one after another, all with freshly painted signs and spotless windows. According to the land registry they were paid for in cash by a Budapest company whose partners no one knows. None seems to have many customers; all stay open late.
G3Facciate.3.easy: **NEW SHOPS, FEW CUSTOMERS.** In the last month some new shops have opened in {0}, one after another, all with freshly painted signs and perfect windows. According to the land office, a Budapest company paid for them in cash, but no one knows who its partners are. None of the shops seems to have many customers, but they all stay open late.
G3Facciate.3.short: **NEW SHOPS, FEW CUSTOMERS.** New shops in {0}, paid in cash by a mysterious Budapest company. Few customers, yet they stay open late.

G3Facciate.4.full: Dr Lukács, asked by this newspaper, has no doubt: they are fronts for the Circle of the Last Hour, behind which the spiritualist society carries on its activities away from prying eyes. The Circle, asked in its turn, replied with a black-edged card: "Trade, too, is a form of consolation."
G3Facciate.4.easy: Dr Lukács, interviewed by this newspaper, is sure: these shops are a cover for the Circle of the Last Hour, which carries on its activities behind them in secret. The Circle replied with a black-bordered card: "Trade is also a way to console."
G3Facciate.4.short: Lukács says they are fronts for the Circle. The Circle replies: "Trade, too, is a form of consolation."

G3Facciate.5.full: In Public Library circles there is talk of a French booklet from 1827, once owned by a notable family, whose last pages are said to be of some interest for the history of the Circle. The librarian declines to comment.
G3Facciate.5.easy: At the Public Library there is talk of a French booklet from 1827, once owned by an important family, whose last pages are said to be of interest for the history of the Circle. The librarian declines to comment.
G3Facciate.5.short: At the library there is talk of a French booklet with interesting pages about the Circle.

G3Facciate.6.full: At the National Bank, meanwhile, the oldest account in town has recorded unusual movements in the last month. The manager reminds readers that banking secrecy is sacred, like that of the confessional.
G3Facciate.6.easy: At the National Bank, meanwhile, the oldest account in town has shown unusual activity in the last month. The manager reminds readers that bank secrecy is sacred, like the secrecy of confession.
G3Facciate.6.short: The National Bank's oldest account has shown odd activity. The manager will not talk.

G3Facciate.7.full: Finally, there is a rumour of a phonograph recording made in secret during a séance of the Circle. Those who claim to have heard it swear that one of the voices says the name of a living person.
G3Facciate.7.easy: Finally, there is a rumour of a phonograph recording made in secret at one of the Circle's séances. Those who say they have heard it swear that one of the voices speaks the name of a living person.
G3Facciate.7.short: There is talk of a secret recording of the Circle, in which a voice speaks a living person's name.

G3Facciate.9.full: Goes into one of the new shops to buy something.

G3Facciate.10.full: Writes to the Gazette in support of Dr Lukács.

G3Facciate.11.full: The shop sells gloves. The shop girl is very kind, pale, and in no hurry. While you try on a pair of grey gloves, three knocks come from the back room, one, two, one; the shop girl smiles and says it is the cat. You leave with the new gloves. They are cold, and stay cold all winter.
G3Facciate.11.easy: The shop sells gloves. The shop assistant is very kind, pale, and in no hurry. While you try on a pair of grey gloves, three knocks come from the back room, one, two, one; the assistant smiles and says it is the cat. You leave with the new gloves. They are cold, and stay cold all winter.
G3Facciate.11.short: You buy gloves. Three knocks come from the back: "It's the cat." The gloves stay cold all winter.

G3Facciate.13.full: The letter appears on Tuesday, on page three, signed with the family's full name. Dr Lukács cuts it out and pins it up in his study. The Circle does not reply. But on Wednesday, in front of every new shop, there is a vase of fresh black carnations, one per window.
G3Facciate.13.easy: The letter comes out on Tuesday, on page three, signed with the family's full name. Dr Lukács cuts it out and pins it up in his office. The Circle does not reply. But on Wednesday, outside every new shop, there is a vase of fresh black carnations, one in each window.
G3Facciate.13.short: The letter appears in the Gazette. The Circle does not reply, but black carnations appear outside every new shop.

G3Facciate.15.full: From the **The Cost of Disease** Scenario Box, take the **5 Suspicious Buildings**, shuffle them and place **{0}** of them next to the Village Chronicle, shop side up. They are village Locations like any other. Return the others to the box without looking at them.

G3Facciate.16.full: **Unmasking:** when, in the same Round, at least two different players have placed a piece on the same Suspicious Building, flip it at the end of the Round: the back says what it was hiding, and those who helped unmask it gain the VP shown.

G3R2.2.full: Turn to **page 11** of the Village Chronicle, **The Cost of Disease** section ({icon:S1_ScenarioIcon}). The Suspicious Buildings stay next to the Chronicle.

G3R2.4.full: The Telegraph is almost finished. When you complete a **C** Experiment, you may give up its VP to finish it:

G3R2.10.full: The first player who sends one of their pieces to the Hospital

G3R2.13.full: The first player who sends one of their pieces to the Chemist

G3R2.16.full: The first player who sends one of their pieces to the Factory

G3R2.25.full: Will the Circle's fronts withstand the heirs' scrutiny?

round.G3R2.end.full: The Middle Years of the Third Generation have ended.

round.G3R2.then.full: Flip the unmasked Suspicious Buildings, then continue with the Storybook.

G3Confessione.2.full: In the Hospital's common ward, between a consumptive and a man with both legs in plaster, there is an old man whose lungs have been burned by fifty years at the forge. He breathes with a whistle, and every breath costs him. It is Jóska, the smith. He asked the nuns to send for someone from the estate, and the nuns, scandalised, obeyed.
G3Confessione.2.easy: In the Hospital's common ward, between a man with consumption and a man with both legs in plaster, lies an old man whose lungs have been burned by fifty years at the forge. He breathes with a whistle, and every breath is an effort. It is Jóska, the smith. He asked the nuns to send for someone from the estate, and the nuns, shocked, did as he asked.
G3Confessione.2.short: In hospital lies Jóska, the old smith, his lungs burned by the forge. He has asked to see someone from the estate.

G3Confessione.3.full: "The family of the coin," he says when he sees you, and smiles with his gums. "I wanted you to know, before the priest."
G3Confessione.3.easy: "The family of the coin," he says when he sees you, smiling with his gums. "I wanted you to know, before the priest."
G3Confessione.3.short: "The family of the coin. I wanted you to know, before the priest."

G3Confessione.4.full: "You of all people," he says when he sees you, with a sort of satisfaction. "I wanted you to know. So you carry it around with you."
G3Confessione.4.easy: "You, of all people," he says when he sees you, almost pleased. "I wanted you to know. So you carry it with you."
G3Confessione.4.short: "You, of all people. I wanted you to know. So you carry it with you."

G3Confessione.5.full: For twenty years, from 1858 to 1878, Jóska knocked inside the walls of half the village. Mr Garai paid him, the one with the carnation; Madame had taught him. Cavities, padded hammers, ropes going down to the cellar. The widows wept on the other side of the wall, and he, in the cellar, wept with them, so as not to get the rhythm wrong.
G3Confessione.5.easy: For twenty years, from 1858 to 1878, Jóska knocked inside the walls of half the village. Mr Garai paid him, the man with the carnation; Madame had taught him. Gaps in walls, padded hammers, ropes running down to the cellar. The widows wept on the other side of the wall, and he, in the cellar, wept with them, so as not to lose the rhythm.
G3Confessione.5.short: For twenty years Jóska knocked inside the village walls, paid by Garai. The widows wept, and he wept with them.

G3Confessione.6.full: "But at the estate, never," he says, clutching your sleeve. "And the first night, the one in '48, I was six. They were knocking from the big house, and I answered. I was the one who answered. Not the one who knocked."
G3Confessione.6.easy: "But at the estate, never," he says, gripping your sleeve. "And the first night, the one in '48, I was six. They were knocking from the big house, and I answered. I was the one who answered. Not the one who knocked."
G3Confessione.6.short: "But never at the estate. On the first night I was six. I answered. I wasn't the one knocking."

G3Confessione.8.full: You send for a notary: the confession must be put in writing.

G3Confessione.9.full: You ask him who was knocking at the estate, then.

G3Confessione.10.full: You hold his hand until he falls asleep.

G3Confessione.11.full: The notary arrives within the hour, with ink and two witnesses. Jóska dictates everything, short of breath: the dates, the houses, the payments, the names. He signs with a cross, because he never learned to write, and the cross comes out crooked. The notary seals the confession and hands you a copy.
G3Confessione.11.easy: The notary comes within the hour, with ink and two witnesses. Jóska dictates it all, short of breath: the dates, the houses, the payments, the names. He signs with a cross, because he never learned to write, and the cross comes out crooked. The notary seals the confession and gives you a copy.
G3Confessione.11.short: Jóska dictates it all to the notary, and signs with a crooked cross. You have a copy.

G3Confessione.12.full: Dr Lukács, when he reads it, says nothing for a long moment. Then he shakes your hand, hard, like a man who at last holds proof that will stand up in court.
G3Confessione.12.easy: When Dr Lukács reads it, he says nothing for a long moment. Then he shakes your hand, hard, like a man who at last has proof that will stand up in court.
G3Confessione.12.short: Lukács shakes your hand: at last, proof that will stand up in court.

G3Confessione.14.full: The old man looks at you, then at the ward wall, white with whitewash, as if he expected an answer from there. "Nobody living," he says. "I knew it even as a child. The living knock with their knuckles. That one knocked with something else."
G3Confessione.14.easy: The old man looks at you, then at the whitewashed ward wall, as if expecting an answer from it. "No one living," he says. "I knew it even as a boy. The living knock with their knuckles. That one knocked with something else."
G3Confessione.14.short: "No one living. The living knock with their knuckles. That one knocked with something else."

G3Confessione.15.full: He dies that night, say the nuns, without suffering. The nun on duty says she heard, around three, slow and regular knocks in the wall behind his bed, and had the impression that the old man, before passing away, answered.
G3Confessione.15.easy: He dies that night, the nuns say, without suffering. The nun on duty says that around three she heard slow, regular knocks in the wall behind his bed, and had the feeling that the old man answered before he passed away.
G3Confessione.15.short: He dies that night. The nun hears knocking in the wall, and thinks the old man answers.

G3Confessione.17.full: You hold his hand. It is hard as leather, full of burn scars, and at the end it grows light. The old smith falls asleep in the middle of a sentence, his mouth open, and does not wake again.
G3Confessione.17.easy: You hold his hand. It is hard as leather, covered in burn scars, and at the end it grows light. The old smith falls asleep in the middle of a sentence, his mouth open, and never wakes.
G3Confessione.17.short: You hold his hand. He falls asleep mid-sentence, and never wakes.

G3Confessione.18.full: At the funeral, the next day, there are only a nun, a shop boy and you. As the gravedigger lowers the coffin, three faint knocks come from inside, one, two, one: the child's game. The gravedigger crosses himself and says it is the earth settling.
G3Confessione.18.easy: At the funeral the next day there are only a nun, an errand boy and you. As the gravedigger lowers the coffin, three soft knocks come from inside, one, two, one: the child's game. The gravedigger crosses himself and says it is the earth settling.
G3Confessione.18.short: At the funeral, three knocks come from the coffin: one, two, one. The child's game.

G3Fosforo.2.full: The Chemist on the square has windows full of coloured phials, a brass scale and a poisons register, as the law requires: whoever buys arsenic, strychnine or white phosphorus must sign, with their name and the reason for the purchase. The chemist is a fussy, talkative man, and he keeps the register like a prayer book.
G3Fosforo.2.easy: The Chemist on the square has windows full of coloured bottles, a brass scale and a poisons register, as the law demands: anyone who buys arsenic, strychnine or white phosphorus must sign, with their name and the reason for buying. The chemist is a fussy, chatty man, and keeps the register like a prayer book.
G3Fosforo.2.short: The chemist keeps a poisons register: anyone buying arsenic or phosphorus must sign.

G3Fosforo.3.full: He shows it to you proudly, leafing back through it. White phosphorus, every month, for thirty years: the Circle's funeral parlour ("for lighting the chapels"), a Viennese photographer ("for plates"), a certain Mrs Vámos ("for rheumatism"). And, more often than all of them, in a handwriting you know, your family's estate: "for experiments".
G3Fosforo.3.easy: He shows it to you proudly, leafing backwards. White phosphorus, every month, for thirty years: the Circle's funeral parlour ("to light the chapels"), a Viennese photographer ("for plates"), a certain Mrs Vámos ("for rheumatism"). And, more often than any of them, in handwriting you know, your family's estate: "for experiments".
G3Fosforo.3.short: White phosphorus for thirty years: the Circle's funeral parlour, a photographer, Mrs Vámos. And, most of all, your family.

G3Fosforo.6.full: You buy something too, and sign.

G3Fosforo.7.full: You tear out the pages with your family's name.

G3Fosforo.8.full: The chemist does not want to sell it: it is a legal document. Then he sees the sum you offer, and discovers that the law, after all, only requires that the register exist, not where. You leave with the register under your arm, wrapped in brown paper.
G3Fosforo.8.easy: The chemist will not sell it: it is a legal document. Then he sees how much you are offering, and decides that the law, after all, only says the register must exist, not where. You leave with it under your arm, wrapped in brown paper.
G3Fosforo.8.short: The chemist will not sell it. Then he sees what you offer, and changes his mind.

G3Fosforo.9.full: At home you read it all. The Circle bought enough phosphorus to make every ghost in the province glow. Your family, though, bought twice as much.
G3Fosforo.9.easy: At home you read it all. The Circle bought enough phosphorus to make every ghost in the province glow. Your family, though, bought twice as much.
G3Fosforo.9.short: The Circle bought a lot of phosphorus. Your family bought twice as much.

G3Fosforo.10.full: If you can, pay $2: gain 3VP. Otherwise gain 1VP.

G3Fosforo.11.full: The chemist weighs the powder with an ivory spoon, wraps it, has you sign. You write your name under those of your parents and grandparents, in the same column, under "for experiments". For a moment it feels as if you are continuing a letter begun by others.
G3Fosforo.11.easy: The chemist weighs the powder with an ivory spoon, wraps it and has you sign. You write your name under those of your parents and grandparents, in the same column, under "for experiments". For a moment it is like carrying on a letter someone else began.
G3Fosforo.11.short: You sign below your parents and grandparents, under "for experiments".

G3Fosforo.13.full: You wait for the chemist to go into the back room, and tear out the pages one by one, slowly, along the binding. There are eleven of them. You burn them that same evening in the laboratory stove, where the paper, soaked in who knows what, burns with a green flame.
G3Fosforo.13.easy: You wait for the chemist to go into the back room, and tear the pages out one by one, slowly, along the binding. There are eleven. You burn them that same evening in the laboratory stove, where the paper, soaked in who knows what, burns with a green flame.
G3Fosforo.13.short: You tear out eleven pages and burn them. They burn with a green flame.

G3Fosforo.14.full: The next day the chemist reports the theft to the gendarmes. The missing pages, he says, were the Circle's. He remembers nothing else.
G3Fosforo.14.easy: The next day the chemist reports the theft to the gendarmes. The missing pages, he says, were the Circle's. He remembers nothing else.
G3Fosforo.14.short: The chemist reports the theft. But he only remembers the Circle's pages.

G3Corrente.2.full: The Factory, on the riverbank, makes nothing: it is the power station of {0}, with two turbines as big as carriages, a red-brick chimney and a very young engineer, from Budapest, who loves it as one loves a person. He shows you the dynamos, the valves, the wires running off towards the town.
G3Corrente.2.easy: The Factory, on the riverbank, makes nothing: it is the power station of {0}, with two turbines the size of carriages, a red-brick chimney and a very young engineer from Budapest who loves it as one loves a person. He shows you the dynamos, the valves, the wires running off into town.
G3Corrente.2.short: The Factory is the power station. The young engineer loves it like a person.

G3Corrente.3.full: He knows about your machine: everyone does. "A telegraph that talks to the dead," he says, amused. "It would be the power station's first customer who doesn't complain about the bills." Then, more seriously: "A machine like that needs clean, steady current. I can run a cable to the estate for you. Or, if you prefer, to the town hall."
G3Corrente.3.easy: He knows about your machine: everyone does. "A telegraph that talks to the dead," he says, amused. "The first customer who wouldn't complain about the bills." Then, more seriously: "A machine like that needs clean, steady current. I can run a cable to the estate for you. Or, if you prefer, to the town hall."
G3Corrente.3.short: "Your telegraph needs clean current. I can run a cable to the estate, or to the town hall."

G3Corrente.5.full: You pay for the cable to the estate.

G3Corrente.6.full: You have him show you the power station at night.

G3Corrente.7.full: You decline: the estate will stay in the dark.

G3Corrente.8.full: The poles arrive in a week, the cable in two. On the evening the current is switched on at the estate, every bulb lights up at once, and for a moment the house looks like an ocean liner in the night. Then all the lights flicker together, three times: one, two, one. The engineer says it is normal. He says it twice.
G3Corrente.8.easy: The poles arrive in a week, the cable in two. On the evening they switch the current on at the estate, every bulb lights at once, and for a moment the house looks like an ocean liner in the night. Then all the lights flicker together, three times: one, two, one. The engineer says it is normal. He says it twice.
G3Corrente.8.short: The current reaches the estate. The lights flicker three times: one, two, one. "It's normal," says the engineer. Twice.

G3Corrente.10.full: At night the power station is a cathedral: the turbines turn in the dark, the work lamps cast long shadows, and the hum of the dynamos gets into your teeth. The engineer shows you, on the meter panel, a needle that should not move and that instead, every night between three and four, jerks back and forth, like a finger looking for a letter.
G3Corrente.10.easy: At night the power station is a cathedral: the turbines turn in the dark, the work lamps throw long shadows, and the hum of the dynamos gets into your teeth. The engineer shows you, on the meter board, a needle that should not move and that instead, every night between three and four, jerks back and forth, like a finger searching for a letter.
G3Corrente.10.short: At night, a needle in the power station moves by itself, in jerks, like a finger searching for a letter.

G3Corrente.11.full: "I've changed the meter three times," he says. "I thought of a fault, of someone stealing current, of a mouse. Then I started writing the movements down." He shows you the notebook. They are letters. And the letters, put in a row, spell your family's name.
G3Corrente.11.easy: "I've changed the meter three times," he says. "I thought it was a fault, someone stealing current, a mouse. Then I started writing down the movements." He shows you the notebook. They are letters. And the letters, in a row, spell your family's name.
G3Corrente.11.short: The engineer wrote down the movements. They are letters, and they spell your family's name.

G3Corrente.13.full: You thank the engineer and tell him the estate has always run on oil lamps, and will go on doing so. He shrugs, disappointed as a rejected lover. A week later he runs the cable to the town hall.
G3Corrente.13.easy: You thank the engineer and tell him the estate has always used oil lamps and always will. He shrugs, as disappointed as a rejected lover. A week later the cable goes to the town hall.
G3Corrente.13.short: You decline. The cable goes to the town hall.

G3Corrente.14.full: The estate remains the only dark house on the hill. In the evening, from the town, people look at it and cross themselves, as they used to.
G3Corrente.14.easy: The estate stays the only dark house on the hill. In the evening, from town, people look at it and cross themselves, as in the old days.
G3Corrente.14.short: The estate is the only dark house on the hill. From town, people cross themselves.

G3Offerta.2.full: In the National Bank manager's office, sitting in the manager's armchair, there is a tall, thin, extremely elegant gentleman with a black carnation in his buttonhole. He introduces himself as Mr Garai, president of the Circle of the Last Hour. He looks no more than fifty. He has the same handwriting, he tells you with amusement, as his father and his grandfather.
G3Offerta.2.easy: In the National Bank manager's office, in the manager's armchair, sits a tall, thin, very elegant gentleman with a black carnation in his buttonhole. He introduces himself as Mr Garai, president of the Circle of the Last Hour. He looks no more than fifty. He has the same handwriting, he tells you with amusement, as his father and his grandfather.
G3Offerta.2.short: In the bank manager's chair sits Mr Garai, president of the Circle. He looks about fifty.

G3Offerta.3.full: He knows your family's debts down to the last penny, and he will pay them all, today. In exchange he asks one thing only: the plans of the Telegraph of the Dead, the three ink drawings made by the founder. "They were meant for us, originally," he says. "Your ancestor kept them for himself. We forgave him. But we would like them back."
G3Offerta.3.easy: He knows your family's debts down to the last penny, and he will pay them all, today. In return he wants one thing: the plans of the Telegraph of the Dead, the three ink drawings made by the founder. "They were meant for us, to begin with," he says. "Your ancestor kept them. We have forgiven him. But we would like them back."
G3Offerta.3.short: He will pay all your debts, in return for the Telegraph plans. "They were meant for us to begin with."

G3Offerta.5.full: You accept: you give him the plans.

G3Offerta.7.full: You give him fake plans, copied with a few mistakes.

G3Offerta.8.full: Mr Garai receives the drawings with an almost religious respect, rolls them up, ties them with black ribbon. The bank manager signs the discharge of the debts with trembling hands. As you leave, you notice that there is also a small extra deposit in your account, "for seventy years' interest".
G3Offerta.8.easy: Mr Garai takes the drawings with almost religious respect, rolls them up and ties them with black ribbon. The bank manager signs the release of the debts with shaking hands. As you leave, you notice a small extra deposit in your account too, "for seventy years' interest".
G3Offerta.8.short: Garai takes the drawings like a relic. There is also a deposit in your account, "for seventy years' interest".

G3Offerta.10.full: Mr Garai does not insist. He gets up, pulls on his gloves, wishes you luck with the Telegraph. "You will finish it," he says. "It's in the blood. And when you switch it on, it will be you who calls us." The door closes by itself behind him. The manager, pale, asks you if you would like to renegotiate the mortgage.
G3Offerta.10.easy: Mr Garai does not insist. He stands, pulls on his gloves, and wishes you luck with the Telegraph. "You will finish it," he says. "It's in the blood. And when you switch it on, you will be the ones calling us." The door closes by itself behind him. The manager, pale, asks if you would like to renegotiate the mortgage.
G3Offerta.10.short: "You will finish it. It's in the blood. And when you switch it on, you'll be calling us." The door closes by itself.

G3Offerta.12.full: You spend three nights copying the drawings, introducing tiny mistakes, a reversed winding, a valve in the wrong place. Mr Garai examines them at length, with a monocle, then rolls them up and pays. At the door he turns. "The dead will check," he says, smiling. "They're very particular." That night, in the laboratory, you find your faulty copies on the desk, corrected in pencil, point by point.
G3Offerta.12.easy: You spend three nights copying the drawings, slipping in tiny mistakes, a reversed winding, a valve in the wrong place. Mr Garai studies them for a long time, through a monocle, then rolls them up and pays. At the door he turns. "The dead will check," he says, smiling. "They're very fussy." That night, in the laboratory, you find your faulty copies on the desk, corrected in pencil, point by point.
G3Offerta.12.short: You give him faulty copies. "The dead will check," says Garai. That night you find them on your desk, corrected in pencil.

G3Stanze.2.full: At the Builder's Office the old foreman, who built the new shops on the square on behalf of "a Budapest company", calls you into his office and shuts the door. He has built many strange things, he says, in forty years in the trade; but never so many all at once.
G3Stanze.2.easy: At the Builder's Office the old foreman, who built the new shops on the square for "a Budapest company", calls you into his office and shuts the door. He has built many strange things, he says, in forty years of work; but never so many at once.
G3Stanze.2.short: The foreman who built the new shops calls you into his office. He has something to show you.

G3Stanze.3.full: He shows you the plans. Every shop has an extra room, behind the back room, windowless, with a door hidden in the wallpaper. And from every room a brass tube runs, under the street, to the Circle's Temple. "For talking to each other," he says. "Like on a ship. But who's talking? And to whom?"
G3Stanze.3.easy: He shows you the plans. Every shop has an extra room, behind the back room, with no windows and a door hidden in the wallpaper. And from every room a brass tube runs under the street to the Circle's Temple. "For talking to each other," he says. "Like on a ship. But who is talking? And to whom?"
G3Stanze.3.short: Every shop has a hidden room, with a brass tube running to the Circle's Temple. "But who is talking? And to whom?"

G3Stanze.5.full: You take the plans to Dr Lukács.

G3Stanze.6.full: You take them to the Circle, and ask what they are worth.

G3Stanze.7.full: You go into one of the hidden rooms at night.

G3Stanze.8.full: Dr Lukács spreads the plans out on his study table, weighs them down with four books and looks at them in silence, like a general looking at a map. "The widows upstairs," he says at last, "and the tubes downstairs. That's how they knew everything." He shakes your hand. "This will stand up in court."
G3Stanze.8.easy: Dr Lukács spreads the plans on his office table, holds them down with four books and studies them in silence, like a general studying a map. "The widows upstairs," he says at last, "and the tubes downstairs. That's how they knew everything." He shakes your hand. "This will stand up in court."
G3Stanze.8.short: "Widows upstairs, tubes downstairs," says Lukács. "That's how they knew everything. This will stand up in court."

G3Stanze.10.full: Mr Garai receives you in his study, looks at the plans without touching them and smiles. "They are worth as much as your silence," he says, and writes a figure on a card. It is a generous figure. The plans end up in the Circle's stove, in front of you. The foreman, the following month, retires, with a new house on the lakeshore.
G3Stanze.10.easy: Mr Garai receives you in his study, looks at the plans without touching them and smiles. "They are worth as much as your silence," he says, and writes a figure on a card. It is a generous figure. The plans go into the Circle's stove, in front of you. The next month the foreman retires, with a new house by the lake.
G3Stanze.10.short: "They're worth as much as your silence," says Garai, and pays well. The plans go into the stove.

G3Stanze.12.full: The door in the wallpaper of the glove shop opens with a push. The hidden room is small, dark, with a chair, a little table and the mouth of a brass tube. You sit down. You put your ear close. From the tube comes a murmur, many voices at once, as in a drawing room full of people; then a single voice, very close, which says your name and asks whether the room is to your liking.
G3Stanze.12.easy: The door in the glove shop's wallpaper opens with a push. The hidden room is small and dark, with a chair, a little table and the mouth of a brass tube. You sit down. You put your ear to it. From the tube comes a murmur, many voices at once, like a drawing room full of people; then a single voice, very close, which says your name and asks whether the room is to your liking.
G3Stanze.12.short: In the hidden room you put your ear to the tube. A voice says your name, and asks if the room is to your liking.

G3Telegrafo.2.full: You solder the last wire with trembling hands. Before you can even turn the switch, the Telegraph turns itself on: the glass jars light up one after another, like the windows of a house at sunset, and a low hum fills the laboratory, the estate, perhaps the whole town.
G3Telegrafo.2.easy: You solder the last wire with shaking hands. Before you can turn the switch, the Telegraph turns on by itself. The glass jars light up one after another, like the windows of a house at sunset, and a low hum fills the laboratory, the estate, maybe the whole town.
G3Telegrafo.2.short: At the last wire the Telegraph switches itself on, and a hum fills the estate, perhaps the town.

G3Telegrafo.3.full: The needle rises, hesitates, then begins to tap on the bone keys, slowly, decisively. It taps out a name: your family's. Then it stops, and waits, like someone who has rung a doorbell.
G3Telegrafo.3.easy: The needle rises, waits a moment, then begins to tap on the bone keys, slowly and surely. It writes a name: your family's. Then it stops and waits, like someone who has rung a doorbell.
G3Telegrafo.3.short: The needle taps out your family's name, then waits, like someone who has rung a doorbell.

G3Telegrafo.4.full: You do not gain the Experiment's VP: instead, gain 5VP.

G3Conteggio.2.full: How many Suspicious Buildings have been unmasked so far?

G3Conteggio.3.full: **THE SCANDAL OF THE CIRCLE.** The Gazette publishes on its front page, across six columns, the evidence gathered by Dr Lukács: the smith's receipts, the unmasked shops, the confessions of two former members. Membership of the Circle of the Last Hour collapses within a week; on the square someone throws stones at its windows.
G3Conteggio.3.easy: **THE SCANDAL OF THE CIRCLE.** The Gazette publishes on its front page, across six columns, the evidence found by Dr Lukács: the blacksmith's receipts, the exposed shops, the confessions of two former members. In a week almost everyone leaves the Circle of the Last Hour, and on the square someone throws stones at its windows.
G3Conteggio.3.short: **THE SCANDAL OF THE CIRCLE.** The Gazette prints Lukács's evidence. Within a week the Circle loses its members, and stones fly on the square.

G3Conteggio.4.full: Madame Vámos, summoned by the magistrate, does not appear. They say she has packed her bags; they also say she has no bags to pack.
G3Conteggio.4.easy: Madame Vámos is called by the judge, but she does not come. Some say she has packed her bags. Others say she has no bags to pack.

G3Conteggio.5.full: At the estate, that night, the knocking on the walls is fainter than usual. Almost shy.
G3Conteggio.5.easy: That night, at the estate, the knocking on the walls is softer than usual. Almost shy.

G3Conteggio.7.full: No one has touched the fronts. The Circle's shops stay open late, with spotless windows and few customers; Dr Lukács writes furious letters to the Gazette, which does not publish them.
G3Conteggio.7.easy: No one has touched the fake shops. The Circle's shops stay open late, with perfect windows and few customers. Dr Lukács writes angry letters to the Gazette, but the Gazette does not print them.
G3Conteggio.7.short: No one has touched the fronts, and the Gazette does not print Lukács's furious letters.

G3Conteggio.8.full: The Circle, in silence, gives thanks: one morning each heir finds a fresh black carnation on the doorstep.
G3Conteggio.8.easy: The Circle, without a word, says thank you: one morning each heir finds a fresh black carnation in front of the door.

G3Conteggio.9.full: One front has fallen, and what was behind it went round the town in a day. But the others are still standing, and the Circle denies everything with great dignity.
G3Conteggio.9.easy: One fake shop has been exposed, and in a day the whole town knows what it was hiding. But the others are still open, and the Circle denies everything with great dignity.
G3Conteggio.9.short: One front has fallen, but the others hold, and the Circle denies everything.

G3Conteggio.10.full: {0} no longer knows whom to believe. People go to mass on Sundays and to séances on Thursdays, just to be safe.
G3Conteggio.10.easy: In {0} no one knows whom to believe any more. To be safe, people go to mass on Sunday and to séances on Thursday.

G3Conteggio.11.full: Among the documents passing from hand to hand in town is a copy of the confession of Jóska, the old smith, signed with a crooked cross and countersigned by a notary: twenty years of knocking in walls, paid by the day. Whoever reads it to the end always stops at the last line, the one about the first night, and reads it again.
G3Conteggio.11.easy: Among the documents passing from hand to hand in town is a copy of old Jóska the smith's confession, signed with a crooked cross and witnessed by a notary: twenty years of knocking in walls, paid by the day. Everyone who reads it to the end stops at the last line, the one about the first night, and reads it again.
G3Conteggio.11.short: Jóska's confession goes round the town. Everyone stops at the last line, the one about the first night.

G3Conteggio.12.full: The chemist on the square, meanwhile, tells all his customers that his poisons register has suddenly become the most interesting book in town.
G3Conteggio.12.easy: Meanwhile the chemist on the square tells all his customers that his poisons register has suddenly become the most interesting book in town.
G3Conteggio.12.short: The chemist tells everyone that his poisons register is the most interesting book in town.

G3Conteggio.13.full: And the engineer from the power station, at the café, shows anyone who asks a notebook full of letters written by a needle that should not move.
G3Conteggio.13.easy: And the engineer from the power station shows anyone at the café who asks a notebook full of letters written by a needle that should not move.
G3Conteggio.13.short: And the engineer shows everyone the notebook written by the needle that should not move.

G3R3.3.full: Open the Village Chronicle to the **Fear of the Unknown** section ({icon:S2_ScenarioIcon}) and turn to **page 11**.

G3R3.4.full: Open the Village Chronicle to the **Fear of the Unknown** section ({icon:S2_ScenarioIcon}) and turn to **page 20**.

G3R3.5.full: The Suspicious Buildings stay next to the Chronicle.

G3R3.16.full: The first player who sends one of their pieces to the Foundry

G3R3.22.full: The first player who sends one of their pieces to the Library

G3R3.25.full: At the end of this Generation, the whole town will sit down around the same table.
G3R3.25.easy: At the end of this Generation, the whole town will sit at the same table.

round.G3R3.end.full: The Late Years of the Third Generation have ended.

round.G3R3.then.full: Perform the End of Round actions, then continue with the Storybook for the Great Séance.

G3Tomba.2.full: The gravedigger now is the son of old Mihály, the gravedigger before him: a man of fifty, big and silent like his father, with the same cap. He takes you to the founder's grave, the family's first, the one where everything began fifty-seven years ago.
G3Tomba.2.easy: The gravedigger now is the son of old Mihály, the gravedigger before him: a man of fifty, big and quiet like his father, with the same cap. He takes you to the founder's grave, the family's first, where it all began fifty-seven years ago.
G3Tomba.2.short: The old gravedigger's son takes you to the founder's grave, where it all began fifty-seven years ago.

G3Tomba.3.full: The brass tube is still open, and round the mound there is a heap of folded notes, some recent, some yellow and crumbling: the post of the living for the dead, which nobody has ever stopped posting.
G3Tomba.3.easy: The brass tube is still open, and around the grave lies a heap of folded notes, some new, some yellow and crumbling: the post of the living for the dead, which no one has ever stopped sending.
G3Tomba.3.short: The tube is still open, surrounded by a heap of notes: the post of the living for the dead.

G3Tomba.4.full: The lead plug that sealed the tube is on the grass, beside the headstone, smooth and shiny as a coin. Nobody touched it: it came out by itself, says the gravedigger, one summer night, with a sound like a champagne cork.
G3Tomba.4.easy: The lead plug that sealed the tube lies on the grass beside the headstone, smooth and shiny as a coin. No one touched it: it came out by itself, says the gravedigger, one summer night, with a pop like a champagne cork.
G3Tomba.4.short: The lead plug lies on the grass. It came out by itself one summer night, like a champagne cork.

G3Tomba.5.full: On the brass tube someone has fitted a new bell, of silver, just like the ones at the Circle's funeral parlour. "He gave them the idea," says the gravedigger, pointing at the headstone. "The first one. The others copied it."
G3Tomba.5.easy: Someone has fitted a new silver bell to the brass tube, just like the ones at the Circle's funeral parlour. "He gave them the idea," says the gravedigger, pointing at the headstone. "The first one. The others copied it."
G3Tomba.5.short: A silver bell sits on the tube, like those at the funeral parlour. "He gave them the idea," says the gravedigger.

G3Tomba.6.full: The headstone is worn by the rain, and the name can barely be read. Beside it, in the grass, there is still the hole of the old brass tube, filled with earth.

FinaleSquarciato.3.full: Dear Doctor, you ask me what happened on the night of 31 December 1905. I will tell you, even though you will not believe me, and even though you need only step out of the sacristy and take a few steps across the square to see it with your own eyes.
FinaleSquarciato.3.easy: Dear Doctor, you ask me what happened on the night of 31 December 1905. I will tell you, even if you will not believe me. And even though you only need to leave the sacristy and walk a little on the square to see it with your own eyes.
FinaleSquarciato.3.short: Dear Doctor, you ask about the night of 31 December 1905. You will not believe me, but you need only step into the square to see.

FinaleSquarciato.4.full: We voted to open. The Telegraph, or the medium, or our joined hands (I no longer know which was the key) turned in the lock, and the veil tore like an old curtain. There was no flash, no thunder. Only a great cold, and then the door of the hall opening by itself, and people coming in. People we knew. People we had buried.
FinaleSquarciato.4.easy: We voted to open. The Telegraph, or the medium, or our joined hands (I no longer know what the key was) turned in the lock, and the veil tore like an old curtain. There was no flash and no thunder. Only a great cold. Then the door of the hall opened by itself, and people came in. People we knew. People we had buried.
FinaleSquarciato.4.short: We voted to open, and the veil tore like an old curtain. In a great cold, people we had buried came in through the door.

FinaleSquarciato.5.full: They stayed. In {0} the dead walk with the living, sit at their tables, vote in the council, complain about the price of bread. At first you could tell them apart: they were paler, quieter, and cast no shadow. Now it is no longer so simple.
